recipes.name: Irish apple cake
recipes.description: A homely spiced apple cake with a tender crumb and crisp sugar top.
ingredients: 2 medium cooking apples, peeled, cored and cut into 1 cm pieces
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Butter and line a 20 cm round cake tin.
Rub butter into flour, baking powder, salt and cinnamon until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Stir in 125 g sugar.
Beat egg with milk. Pour into the dry mixture and stir just until no dry flour remains; fold in apple pieces.
Spread into the tin, level the top and sprinkle with the remaining sugar. Bake 45–50 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out without wet batter. Cool 15 minutes before turning out.
recipes.sides: Serve warm with custard, softly whipped cream or a little butter.
recipes.substitutions: Use a tart firm eating apple if cooking apples are unavailable; reduce sugar slightly for a sweet variety. Ground mixed spice can replace cinnamon.
recipes.storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 2 days or refrigerate for up to 4 days. Rewarm slices briefly in a low oven.
recipes.safety: The centre must be fully baked; check with a skewer rather than relying only on the browned top.

recipes.name: Bacon and cabbage
recipes.description: Salt-cured bacon cooked gently with cabbage and potatoes for a straightforward family meal.
ingredients: 1 small green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: If the bacon label recommends soaking, cover it with cold water for the stated time and discard that water. Put bacon in a pot with onion, carrots and bay leaf; cover with fresh water.

Bring just to a boil, skim, then cover and simmer gently for about 90 minutes, or follow the joint label. Check the centre reaches 70°C for 2 minutes or an equivalent safe time-temperature combination.
Lift the joint to a board and rest under loose foil. Add potatoes to the cooking liquid and simmer 15–20 minutes until tender.
Add cabbage for the final 8–10 minutes so it softens but keeps its shape. Slice bacon across the grain and serve with drained cabbage and potatoes.
recipes.sides: Serve with parsley sauce or mustard and a little of the cooking broth.
recipes.substitutions: Use a labelled gammon joint if Irish bacon is unavailable. Cured joints vary in saltiness, so do not salt the cooking water before tasting.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate meat and vegetables separately, and use within 3 days. Reheat until steaming hot throughout.
recipes.safety: Keep raw pork and its utensils separate from ready-to-eat food. Follow the pack instructions for the joint and verify the thickest part is safely cooked.

recipes.name: Barmbrack
recipes.description: A lightly spiced fruit loaf whose dried fruit is softened in strong tea before baking.
instructions: Soak dried fruit in cooled tea for at least 4 hours, or overnight in the refrigerator. Drain excess tea if the fruit has not absorbed it.
Heat oven to 170°C (150°C fan). Line a 900 g loaf tin with baking paper.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, spice and salt. Stir in the beaten egg and soaked fruit with enough remaining tea to make a thick dropping batter.
Spoon into the tin and bake 50–55 minutes. A skewer inserted in the centre should come out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then on a rack.
recipes.sides: Slice and serve plain or buttered with tea.
recipes.substitutions: Use raisins, sultanas and chopped dates in any combination. Orange zest is a common flavour variation.
recipes.storage: Wrap once completely cool and keep for 3 days; freeze slices for longer storage.
recipes.safety: If soaking fruit overnight, keep it covered in the refrigerator. Cool the loaf before wrapping to prevent condensation.

recipes.name: Beef and stout stew
recipes.description: Slow-braised beef with root vegetables and dark Irish stout; rich, warming everyday cooking.
ingredients: 900 g stewing beef, in 3 cm cubes
instructions: Pat beef dry. Heat oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Brown the beef in batches in a heavy oven-safe pot with oil; transfer each batch to a plate.
Cook onions, carrots and celery in the pot for 6–8 minutes. Stir in flour and tomato paste for one minute, then gradually stir in stout and stock, scraping up browned bits.
Return beef and juices to the pot. Add bay leaves, bring to a simmer, cover and cook in the oven for 2 hours.
Stir in potatoes and cook covered for another 30–40 minutes until beef is fork-tender and potatoes are soft. Remove bay leaves and season after tasting.
recipes.sides: Serve with brown bread, mashed potato or boiled potatoes.
recipes.substitutions: Use another dry stout or replace stout with extra stock and a teaspoon of cider vinegar. Add mushrooms with the potatoes if desired.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 3 days. Reheat gently until steaming hot; add a splash of stock if thick.
recipes.safety: Brown beef in uncrowded batches and keep raw-meat utensils separate. Slow cooking should leave the beef fully tender and hot throughout.

recipes.name: Black pudding and potato hash
recipes.description: Crisp-edged potatoes, onion and cooked black pudding make a filling breakfast or supper hash.
ingredients: 600 g waxy potatoes, cut into 2 cm cubes
250 g black pudding, casing removed if needed and crumbled
instructions: Boil potatoes in unsalted water for 8–10 minutes until just tender but not falling apart. Drain well and let steam dry.
Heat oil in a wide frying pan. Cook onion over medium heat for 6 minutes until soft. Add potatoes in one layer and cook 8–10 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned.
Add black pudding and butter. Break it into small pieces and cook 5–7 minutes, stirring gently until piping hot and crisp at the edges.
Season with pepper, fold in parsley and serve immediately.
recipes.sides: Serve with fried or poached eggs and grilled tomatoes.
recipes.substitutions: White pudding can replace some or all of the black pudding. Use leftover cooked potatoes and reduce their frying time.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 2 days. Reheat in a pan until piping hot throughout.
recipes.safety: Cooked pudding is still perishable; follow its pack instructions and reheat leftovers thoroughly.

recipes.name: Brown soda bread
recipes.description: A quick, no-yeast wholemeal loaf leavened with bicarbonate of soda and cultured buttermilk.
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Dust a baking tray with flour.
Mix both flours, bicarbonate of soda and salt. Make a well and pour in most of the buttermilk.
Bring together quickly with a fork, adding the rest only if dry flour remains. Turn onto a floured surface and shape gently into a round; do not knead.
Set on the tray, cut a deep cross in the top, sprinkle with oats if using, and bake 40–45 minutes. The base should sound hollow when tapped. Cool on a rack.
recipes.sides: Eat fresh with butter, soup or smoked fish.
recipes.substitutions: If buttermilk is unavailable, mix 380 ml milk with 20 ml lemon juice and let stand 10 minutes; texture may differ.
recipes.storage: Best on the day it is baked. Keep wrapped for 2 days; toast day-old slices. Freeze well wrapped.
recipes.safety: Do not taste raw dough. Cool fully before slicing to avoid a gummy centre.

recipes.name: Champ
recipes.description: Creamy mashed potatoes flavoured with spring onions steeped in warm milk and finished with butter.
ingredients: 1 kg floury potatoes, peeled and quartered
instructions: Put potatoes in a pot, cover with cold water and add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer 15–20 minutes until a knife passes through easily.
Meanwhile warm milk with spring onions in a small pan for 3–4 minutes; do not let it boil. Turn off heat and leave to infuse.
Drain potatoes thoroughly and return to the hot pot for 1 minute to dry. Mash until smooth.
Strain or spoon in the warm onion milk gradually, beating until soft. Season, make a well in each serving and add butter.
recipes.sides: Serve alongside bacon, sausages or a simple stew; champ is also served as a dish in its own right.
recipes.substitutions: Use finely chopped scallions or chives if spring onions are unavailable. Add more warm milk for a softer mash.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat covered with a splash of milk until piping hot.
recipes.safety: Take care with hot milk and steam when draining potatoes.

recipes.name: Colcannon
recipes.description: Buttery mashed potatoes folded with tender cabbage or kale, traditionally served around Halloween and throughout the year.
ingredients: 900 g floury potatoes, peeled and quartered
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water for 15–20 minutes until tender. Drain and leave to steam dry.
While potatoes cook, simmer cabbage in a little water for 5–7 minutes until tender. Drain very well.
Warm milk with spring onions. Mash potatoes with butter, then beat in warm milk until creamy.
Fold in cabbage, season with pepper and salt to taste, and serve hot with a small knob of butter.
recipes.sides: Often served with ham, bacon or sausages; a well of melted butter is customary.
recipes.substitutions: Kale can replace cabbage. Leeks may be added, but keep the cabbage or kale as the defining green.
recipes.storage: Cool quickly, refrigerate and use within 3 days. Reheat in a covered pan or microwave, stirring until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Drain greens thoroughly to prevent watery mash; handle hot pans and steam carefully.

recipes.name: Dublin coddle
recipes.description: A gently simmered Dublin one-pot meal of sausages, bacon, onions and potatoes in a light broth.
ingredients: 200 g streaky bacon, cut into pieces
900 g potatoes, peeled and thickly sliced
700 ml low-salt chicken stock or water
instructions: Heat oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Brown sausages in a pot or frying pan for 5–6 minutes; they need not be cooked through. Set aside.
In the same pan cook bacon until it releases some fat. Layer onions and potatoes in an oven-safe casserole, scattering bacon and parsley between layers.
Place sausages on top and pour in stock just to cover the lower layers. Add pepper; avoid salt until tasting because bacon is salty.
Cover and cook in the oven for 75–90 minutes until potatoes are tender and sausages are fully cooked. Check the centre of a sausage reaches 70°C for 2 minutes or equivalent.
recipes.sides: Serve in bowls with crusty bread and extra parsley.
recipes.substitutions: Use vegetable stock or water. Carrots are a modern optional addition rather than part of the classic base.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 3 days. Reheat until piping hot throughout.
recipes.safety: Keep raw sausage separate from ready-to-eat foods. Cook sausages thoroughly; do not rely on browning alone.

recipes.name: Irish fish pie
recipes.description: White fish and smoked haddock in a parsley sauce, baked beneath fluffy mashed potato.
ingredients: 700 g mixed skinless white fish and smoked haddock, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Boil potatoes 15–20 minutes until tender; drain and mash with 20 g butter and a splash of milk.
Arrange fish and peas in a baking dish. Melt remaining butter in a saucepan, stir in flour for one minute, then whisk in milk gradually. Simmer 3–4 minutes until thick.
Stir parsley, lemon juice and pepper into sauce. Taste before adding salt, then pour over the fish.
Spoon mash over the top and roughen with a fork. Bake 30–35 minutes until golden and bubbling; ensure the centre is steaming and fish flakes opaque.
recipes.sides: Serve with peas, carrots or steamed greens.
recipes.substitutions: Use fresh or properly thawed frozen cod, pollock or hake. Replace peas with sweetcorn; adjust salt for smoked fish.
recipes.storage: Cool leftovers promptly, refrigerate and use within 2 days. Reheat until steaming hot throughout; do not reheat repeatedly.
recipes.safety: Thaw frozen fish in the refrigerator. Keep raw fish separate and cook until opaque and easily flaked.

recipes.name: Irish lamb and potato stew
recipes.description: A gentle one-pot family stew with lamb, onion, carrots and potatoes.
ingredients: 700 g stewing lamb, cut into bite-sized pieces
700 g floury potatoes, peeled and cut into large chunks
instructions: Heat oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Pat lamb dry. Brown in batches in a heavy oven-safe pot with oil.
Return lamb to pot. Add onions, carrots, bay leaves and stock. Bring just to a simmer, cover and cook in the oven for 45 minutes.
Add potatoes, cover and cook until lamb is tender and potatoes are cooked, about 50–60 minutes. Check liquid occasionally; add hot water if becoming dry.
Taste, season with pepper and salt if needed, then stir through parsley. Rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve hot with parsley and crusty bread. For a thicker broth, gently press a few cooked potato pieces against the pot; avoid vigorous stirring.
recipes.substitutions: Use mutton or beef stewing pieces with adjusted cooking time. Parsley may be omitted; add a turnip for a regional variation.
recipes.storage: Cool leftovers promptly, refrigerate covered and use within 3 days. Reheat until steaming hot throughout.
recipes.safety: Keep raw lamb separate from ready-to-eat food and wash hands and utensils after handling it.

recipes.name: Leek and potato soup
recipes.description: A simple, filling soup of softened leeks and potatoes, blended or left rustic.
ingredients: 900 ml low-salt vegetable or chicken stock
instructions: Melt butter in a saucepan. Add leeks and cook gently for 8 minutes until soft but not browned.
Add potatoes and stock. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook 18–20 minutes until potatoes break easily.
Blend carefully until smooth, or mash lightly for a chunky soup. Stir in milk and warm gently; do not boil hard.
Season with pepper and serve with chives.
recipes.sides: Serve with brown soda bread or a cheese sandwich.
recipes.substitutions: Use olive oil instead of butter and oat or dairy milk. Add a small handful of parsley before blending.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 3 days. Reheat gently, stirring often, until steaming throughout.
recipes.safety: Blend hot soup in batches with the blender vent open and a towel over the lid; hot liquid expands.

recipes.name: Oat porridge
recipes.description: A comforting bowl of oats simmered slowly until creamy, with a simple choice of sweet or savoury toppings.
ingredients: 600 ml water or milk, or a mix
instructions: Put oats, liquid and salt in a saucepan. Bring slowly to a simmer, stirring so the oats do not catch.
For rolled oats, simmer 5–8 minutes; for pinhead oats, simmer 20–25 minutes and add liquid as needed. Stir regularly until creamy and tender.
Remove from heat and rest 2 minutes. Serve with milk or cream.
recipes.sides: Traditional toppings include a splash of milk, honey, brown sugar or stewed fruit.
recipes.substitutions: Use water for a lighter bowl or dairy-free milk for a dairy-free version. Follow the packet time for the oat cut.
recipes.storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use the next day; loosen with milk or water while reheating.
recipes.safety: Stir carefully as porridge can bubble and spit; avoid leaving it unattended.

recipes.name: Potato farls
recipes.description: Soft potato bread wedges cooked on a dry griddle, often served as part of an Ulster fry.
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15–20 minutes. Drain well and mash until smooth while hot.
Work butter and salt into the mash. Add flour gradually until a soft dough forms; use only enough to stop it sticking.
On a floured surface, pat dough into a 1 cm thick circle and cut into four wedges.
Heat a heavy dry frying pan over medium-low heat. Cook farls 4 minutes per side until browned and cooked through. Split thicker farls to check the centre is hot.
recipes.sides: Serve hot with butter, or alongside eggs, bacon and sausages.
recipes.substitutions: Use leftover dry mashed potato, warming it first. Add a little extra flour only if the dough cannot be handled.
recipes.storage: Eat fresh or refrigerate for up to 2 days. Reheat in a dry pan until hot; farls also freeze well.
recipes.safety: Let potatoes steam dry after draining; wet mash needs excess flour and makes heavy farls.

recipes.name: Potato soup
recipes.description: A thrifty smooth or chunky soup built around potatoes, onion and stock, finished with milk.
instructions: Melt butter in a saucepan and cook onion over low heat for 6–8 minutes until soft.
Add potatoes and stock. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook 18–22 minutes until potatoes are very tender.
Mash for a rustic texture or blend in batches until smooth. Stir in milk and warm gently without boiling.
Season with black pepper and parsley. Add hot water if the soup is thicker than you like.
recipes.sides: Serve with buttered soda bread or crisp rashers.
recipes.substitutions: Replace milk with unsweetened oat milk or omit it and add stock. Add chopped chives at the end.
recipes.storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat slowly, stirring, until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Use care when blending hot soup and keep the blender lid vented.

recipes.name: Salmon and potato fish cakes
recipes.description: Flaked salmon bound with mashed potato, coated in crumbs and shallow-fried until golden.
ingredients: 500 g floury potatoes, peeled and diced
instructions: Simmer potatoes in water for 15 minutes until tender; drain and mash. Poach salmon gently in a little water for 8–10 minutes until opaque and flaking, then cool enough to handle.
Flake salmon, removing skin and pin bones. Fold into mash with herbs, lemon zest and pepper. Shape into 8 cakes and chill for 15 minutes to firm.
Dip each cake in beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs. Heat oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Fry cakes in batches for 3–4 minutes per side until crisp and hot through. Drain briefly on a rack or paper towel.
recipes.sides: Serve with lemon wedges, peas and a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use cooked leftover salmon or canned salmon, drained well. Chives can replace dill.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate cooked cakes promptly and use within 2 days. Reheat in an oven until hot throughout; do not refry repeatedly.
recipes.safety: Keep raw fish chilled and separate. Cook fresh salmon until opaque and easily flaked; chill the mixture before frying if it is soft.

recipes.name: Sausages with champ
recipes.description: A familiar home supper pairing browned pork sausages with creamy spring onion champ.
ingredients: 1 kg floury potatoes, peeled and quartered
instructions: Put potatoes in cold salted water, bring to a boil and simmer 15–20 minutes until tender.
Warm milk with spring onions for 3 minutes over low heat. Drain potatoes and leave them to steam dry, then mash with butter.
Beat warm onion milk into the mash gradually and season with pepper.

While potatoes cook, heat oil in a frying pan and cook sausages over medium-low heat, turning often for 15–18 minutes until evenly browned and cooked through. Check the centre reaches 70°C for 2 minutes or equivalent.
recipes.sides: Serve with onion gravy, peas or braised cabbage.
recipes.substitutions: Use vegetarian sausages and vegetable gravy. Chives can stand in for spring onions.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat sausages and mash until piping hot.
recipes.safety: Cook sausages thoroughly, especially at the centre, and keep raw-meat utensils separate.

recipes.name: Shepherd's pie
recipes.description: Seasoned minced lamb and vegetables baked beneath a browned mashed potato topping.
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil potatoes 15–20 minutes until tender; drain and mash with butter and milk.
Brown lamb in oil in a wide pan, breaking it up. Add onion and carrots and cook 7 minutes until softened.
Stir in tomato paste, stock and Worcestershire sauce. Simmer 12–15 minutes until the filling is moist but not soupy; season and spoon into a baking dish.
Spread mash over the filling and roughen with a fork. Bake 25–30 minutes until golden and bubbling. Rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve with peas, green beans or cabbage.
recipes.substitutions: Use minced beef for cottage pie, though that is a distinct variation. Add peas to the filling in the final few minutes.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 3 days. Reheat portions until steaming hot throughout.
recipes.safety: Brown mince thoroughly and avoid tasting before the filling is fully cooked.

recipes.name: Irish seafood chowder
recipes.description: A creamy coastal soup with white fish, smoked fish, potatoes and a little shellfish.
ingredients: 300 g white fish, skinned and cubed
150 g smoked haddock, skinned and cubed
150 g mussel meat or peeled prawns
instructions: Melt butter in a saucepan and soften leek and celery for 5 minutes without browning.
Add potatoes and fish stock. Simmer 12–15 minutes until potatoes are nearly tender.
Add white fish and smoked haddock and simmer gently for 5 minutes. Stir in mussels or prawns, milk and cream; heat gently until seafood is opaque and steaming. Do not boil hard.
Stir in parsley and pepper. Taste before adding salt, especially when smoked fish is used.
recipes.sides: Serve with brown soda bread and lemon wedges.
recipes.substitutions: Use cod, hake or pollock; replace shellfish with more fish if needed. For a lighter chowder, replace cream with milk.
recipes.storage: Seafood soup is best fresh. Refrigerate promptly and use within 1 day; reheat once gently until piping hot.
recipes.safety: Thaw seafood in the refrigerator, keep it separate from ready-to-eat food and cook until opaque or shells have opened. Discard mussels that remain closed after cooking.

recipes.name: Dulse and potato soup
recipes.description: A simple potato soup with a modest amount of dried dulse for its savoury coastal flavour.
ingredients: 15 g dried dulse, rinsed and chopped
instructions: Rinse dulse well to remove grit and excess salt, then chop finely.
Melt butter in a pot and cook onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add potatoes and stock; simmer covered for 18–20 minutes until tender.
Add dulse and simmer for 3 minutes. Mash roughly or blend carefully in batches.
Stir in milk, warm gently and taste before seasoning. Finish with parsley and black pepper.
recipes.sides: Serve with oatcakes or brown bread.
recipes.substitutions: Use a smaller amount of another food-grade dried seaweed; flavour and saltiness vary. Omit seaweed for plain potato soup.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 2 days. Reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Use seaweed sold for eating and follow its preparation directions. Rinse thoroughly and do not add salt until tasting.

recipes.name: White soda bread
recipes.description: A quick wheaten loaf with a soft crumb, made without yeast and baked soon after mixing.
instructions: Heat oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Dust a baking tray with flour.
Mix flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt. Make a well and add most of the buttermilk.
Mix quickly with a fork until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms; add remaining buttermilk only if dry flour remains. Do not knead.
Shape into a round, cut a deep cross on top and bake 15 minutes. Lower oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and bake another 20–25 minutes. The base should sound hollow when tapped. Cool on a rack.
recipes.sides: Serve warm with butter, soup or smoked salmon.
recipes.substitutions: For a buttermilk substitute, stir 20 ml lemon juice into 330 ml milk and stand 10 minutes. Use wholemeal flour for a denser loaf.
recipes.storage: Best on baking day; keep wrapped for 2 days or freeze. Toast slices that have become firm.
recipes.safety: Work quickly once wet and dry ingredients meet because soda begins reacting. Cool before slicing.

recipes.name: Irish stew with parsley dumplings
recipes.description: A hearty variation on lamb and root vegetable stew with soft dumplings steamed on top.
instructions: Brown lamb in batches in a heavy pot with oil. Add onion, carrots, potatoes, bay and stock. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently 90 minutes until lamb is nearly tender.
Mix flour, suet, parsley and pepper. Add cold water gradually to make a soft dough; divide into 8 balls without compacting them.
Place dumplings on top of the simmering stew with space between. Cover tightly and cook 20–25 minutes without lifting the lid.
Check a dumpling is cooked through in the centre and the lamb is tender. Serve hot.
recipes.sides: The dumplings make this a complete meal; serve with extra greens if desired.
recipes.substitutions: Use vegetable suet for a vegetarian dumpling, though the stew itself contains lamb. Reduce dumpling size if your pot is shallow.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Dumplings soften on storage; reheat stew gently until piping hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw lamb separate and cook the stew thoroughly. Steam escapes when lifting the lid; open it away from your face.

recipes.name: Treacle soda bread
recipes.description: A gently sweet soda loaf with a little treacle, often eaten with butter alongside tea or soup.
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a baking tray.
Mix flours, bicarbonate of soda and salt. Warm treacle briefly so it pours easily, then stir it into buttermilk.
Pour liquid into dry ingredients and mix quickly to a soft dough. Shape into a round without kneading; place on tray and cut a cross in the top.
Sprinkle with oats and bake 35–40 minutes until browned and hollow-sounding underneath. Cool on a rack.
recipes.sides: Serve with salted butter, mature cheese or a bowl of soup.
recipes.substitutions: Use molasses if treacle is unavailable; its stronger flavour may need a little less. Add a handful of raisins for a sweeter tea bread.
recipes.storage: Keep wrapped for 2 days; freeze once cool. Toast slices to refresh.
recipes.safety: Do not taste raw dough. Ensure the centre is baked before cooling and storing.

recipes.name: Full Irish breakfast
recipes.description: A substantial cooked breakfast assembled from rashers, sausages, pudding, eggs, tomatoes and bread; the Ulster fry commonly adds potato bread or farls.
ingredients: 2 potato farls or slices of soda bread
instructions: Warm the oven to 100°C to keep cooked items warm. Heat a large pan over medium heat. Cook sausages, turning often, for 15–18 minutes until cooked through; move to the oven.
Cook rashers and pudding slices in the pan according to their pack directions until browned and hot through. Transfer to the warm tray.
Cook tomatoes cut-side down and mushrooms in the pan for 5–7 minutes until softened. Add a little oil only if the pan is dry.
Fry eggs to preference. Toast or griddle potato farls until hot and lightly browned. Divide everything between warm plates and serve promptly.
recipes.sides: Baked beans and brown soda bread are common additions; tea is a usual accompaniment.
recipes.substitutions: Use either black or white pudding if both are not available. Potato bread and soda bread are regional choices; follow the pudding and sausage packet directions.
recipes.storage: This meal is best freshly cooked. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 2 days; reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw pork separate and cook sausages through to the centre. Do not keep cooked food warm for extended periods; serve soon after cooking.

recipes.name: Carrot and parsnip soup
recipes.description: A smooth, gently sweet soup made with inexpensive winter roots and a little stock.
instructions: Heat oil in a saucepan. Cook onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add carrots, parsnips, cumin if using, and stock. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook 20–25 minutes until the roots are tender.
Blend carefully in batches until smooth. Return to the pan, stir in milk or cream and warm without boiling.
Season with pepper and loosen with hot water if needed.
recipes.sides: Serve with soda bread or oatcakes.
recipes.substitutions: Use sweet potato for part of the parsnip. Omit dairy or use unsweetened oat milk.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate and use within 3 days. Reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Take care blending hot liquid; fill the jug only partway and vent the lid.

recipes.name: Rasher and cabbage skillet
recipes.description: A quick skillet supper of Irish back bacon, cabbage and potatoes, using cooked potatoes to shorten the cooking.
ingredients: 400 g Irish back bacon, cut into strips
instructions: Heat a large pan over medium heat. Cook bacon strips for 5–7 minutes until browned and cooked through; remove to a plate.
Add onion and cook 4 minutes in the pan fat, adding a little oil only if dry. Add cooked potatoes and fry until lightly golden.
Stir in cabbage and stock. Cover and cook 5–7 minutes until cabbage is tender, stirring once.
Return bacon to the pan, heat through and season with pepper. Taste before adding salt.
recipes.sides: Serve with mustard or a spoon of parsley sauce.
recipes.substitutions: Use leftover boiled potatoes and savoy cabbage. Smoked bacon gives a stronger flavour; reduce added salt.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 3 days. Reheat in a pan until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Cook bacon thoroughly and keep raw pork separate from cooked potatoes and vegetables.

recipes.name: Irish oatcakes
recipes.description: Simple savoury oat cakes cooked on a griddle and served with cheese or soup.
instructions: Mix oatmeal, flour and salt in a bowl. Stir melted butter into 100 ml hot water.
Add liquid gradually and mix to a firm dough; add more water by the teaspoon if it crumbles.
Roll between sheets of baking paper to about 4 mm thick and cut into rounds or triangles.
Cook on a lightly greased griddle over low-medium heat for 3–4 minutes per side until dry and lightly browned. Cool on a rack to crisp.
recipes.sides: Serve with cheddar, smoked salmon or soup.
recipes.substitutions: Use all oatmeal for a more rustic texture, adding water gradually. A pinch of black pepper or caraway is optional.
recipes.storage: Cool completely and store airtight for up to 5 days. Re-crisp briefly in a low oven.
recipes.safety: Hot water can make dough warm; let it cool enough to handle before rolling.

recipes.name: Irish pancakes
recipes.description: Thin pan-fried pancakes commonly served with lemon and sugar, especially on Pancake Tuesday.
ingredients: 1 tsp melted butter, plus pan greasing
Lemon wedges and sugar to serve
instructions: Whisk flour and salt in a bowl. Make a well, add egg and about a third of the milk, and whisk to a smooth paste.
Whisk in remaining milk and melted butter. Rest batter 10 minutes if time allows.
Heat a lightly buttered frying pan. Pour in a thin layer of batter, swirl to cover and cook 1–2 minutes until the edges lift.
Flip and cook 30–60 seconds on the second side. Repeat, greasing the pan as needed.
recipes.sides: Serve with lemon juice and sugar, jam or stewed fruit.
recipes.substitutions: Use a suitable unsweetened plant milk; the batter may need a little extra flour. For savoury pancakes omit sugar toppings and fill with cheese or vegetables.
recipes.storage: Best fresh. Stack cooled pancakes between baking paper and refrigerate for 2 days; reheat in a pan.
recipes.safety: Let the pan cool slightly between batches if the butter begins to smoke.

recipes.name: Porter cake
recipes.description: A dark, fruit-rich cake gently simmered with stout and spices before being baked.
instructions: Put stout, butter, sugar and dried fruit in a saucepan. Warm until butter melts and sugar dissolves; simmer gently 5 minutes, then cool completely.
Heat oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Line a deep 20 cm round tin.
Mix flour, baking powder and spice. Stir cooled fruit mixture, orange zest and beaten eggs into the flour until combined.
Spoon into tin and bake 90–100 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. If the top browns early, cover loosely with foil. Cool in tin.
recipes.sides: Serve in thin slices with tea; butter is optional.
recipes.substitutions: Use alcohol-free stout for a non-alcoholic version. Add chopped walnuts if there is no allergy concern.
recipes.storage: Wrap when fully cool; keep in an airtight tin for up to a week or freeze portions.
recipes.safety: Cool the hot fruit mixture fully before adding eggs. Check the centre is baked before storing.

recipes.name: Rhubarb crumble
recipes.description: Tart rhubarb baked under a buttery oat and flour topping, a familiar seasonal home dessert.
ingredients: 700 g rhubarb, trimmed and cut into 3 cm pieces
instructions: Heat oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Put rhubarb in a baking dish with caster sugar and water; toss to coat.
Rub butter into flour until it forms coarse crumbs. Stir in oats and brown sugar.
Scatter topping evenly over rhubarb without pressing it down.
Bake 35–40 minutes until the fruit bubbles at the edges and the topping is golden. Rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve warm with custard, cream or vanilla ice cream.
recipes.substitutions: Use half rhubarb and half apple for a milder filling. Adjust sugar to the tartness of the stalks.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat in an oven until hot.
recipes.safety: Trim and discard rhubarb leaves; they are not edible. Use only the stalks.

recipes.name: Bacon and cabbage soup
recipes.description: A light broth soup using bacon, potatoes and cabbage for an economical lunch.
instructions: Put bacon in a pot over medium heat and cook 5 minutes until it releases fat. Add onion and carrots; cook 5 minutes.
Add potatoes and stock. Bring to a simmer and cook 18–20 minutes until potatoes are nearly tender.
Stir in cabbage and cook 5–7 minutes until soft. Check the bacon is hot and cooked through.
Season with pepper, taste before adding salt, and finish with parsley.
recipes.sides: Serve with brown bread or oatcakes.
recipes.substitutions: Use leftover cooked bacon, adding it with the cabbage. Replace cabbage with kale and simmer until tender.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate and use within 3 days. Reheat until bubbling and steaming throughout.
recipes.safety: Keep raw bacon separate and cook thoroughly; use low-salt stock because bacon is salty.

recipes.name: Honey-glazed baked ham
recipes.description: A boiled then oven-glazed ham joint for a Sunday meal or cold slices through the week.
instructions: If the label advises soaking, soak the ham as directed and discard the water. Put ham in a pot with onion and carrot; cover with fresh water.
Bring to a gentle simmer, skim and cook according to the joint weight and package instructions. The centre should reach a safe temperature; rest the joint 15 minutes.
Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Remove rind carefully, leaving a thin fat layer, and score the fat in a shallow diamond pattern.
Mix mustard, honey and sugar, brush over ham and roast 20–25 minutes until glazed. Rest 15 minutes before slicing.
recipes.sides: Serve hot with cabbage and potatoes, or cool and serve in sandwiches.
recipes.substitutions: Use maple syrup instead of honey. Glaze with mustard and brown sugar alone for a sharper finish.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly, use within 3 days and keep sliced ham covered. Reheat hot portions until steaming.
recipes.safety: Follow the cured joint pack directions and check the thickest part with a food thermometer. Keep raw pork separate.

recipes.name: Dublin Bay prawns with garlic butter
recipes.description: Sweet langoustines cooked briefly and served with parsley and lemon butter.
ingredients: 500 g raw Dublin Bay prawns (langoustines), thawed if frozen
instructions: Rinse prawns under cold running water and pat dry. Heat a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Melt half the butter. Add prawns in a single layer and cook 3–4 minutes, turning once, until shells turn pink and flesh is opaque.
Lower heat. Add remaining butter, garlic and parsley; toss for 30 seconds until fragrant. Do not let garlic brown.
Season with pepper, squeeze over lemon and serve immediately.
recipes.sides: Serve with brown bread to mop up butter and a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use shell-on large prawns if langoustines are unavailable; adjust cooking time to size.
recipes.storage: Seafood is best immediately. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 1 day; reheat gently once.
recipes.safety: Keep raw shellfish separate, thaw in the refrigerator and cook until opaque. Discard any shellfish with an unpleasant smell.

recipes.name: Irish vegetable soup
recipes.description: A flexible everyday soup of onion, carrot, celery and potato simmered in stock and blended smooth.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot. Add onion, carrots and celery and cook over medium-low heat for 7 minutes until softened.
Add potato and stock. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook 20 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Blend until smooth in batches, or leave chunky. Add hot water if needed to reach a spoonable consistency.
Season with pepper and stir in parsley.
recipes.sides: Serve with wheaten bread or a toasted cheese sandwich.
recipes.substitutions: Use turnip, parsnip or a handful of cabbage depending on what is available. Use water plus a little extra seasoning if stock is unavailable.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: When blending hot soup, fill the jug only halfway and vent the lid to release steam.

recipes.name: Soft floury bread rolls
recipes.description: Soft, flour-dusted rolls inspired by Waterford's local blaa tradition; this home recipe is not a specification for the protected regional product.
ingredients: 500 g strong white bread flour, plus dusting
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Rub in butter, then gradually stir in lukewarm water until a soft dough forms.
Knead on a lightly floured surface for 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Put in a lightly oiled bowl, cover and leave in a warm place for about 1 hour, until doubled.
Press dough gently to release large air pockets. Divide into 8 equal pieces and shape each into a round roll. Place close together on a floured tray, cover and prove 30–40 minutes until puffy.
Heat oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Dust tops generously with flour and bake 15–18 minutes until pale gold and hollow-sounding underneath. Cool on a rack.
recipes.sides: Split and fill with butter, rashers or cheese; also serve beside soup.
recipes.substitutions: Use olive oil instead of butter for a dairy-free dough. Flour absorption varies; add water slowly and keep the dough soft rather than stiff.
recipes.storage: Eat on baking day for the softest crumb. Keep covered for 1 day or freeze once cool; thaw and warm briefly.
recipes.safety: Use warm, not hot, water so it does not damage the yeast. Allow the rolls to cool before slicing.

recipes.name: Wheaten scones
recipes.description: Quick wholemeal scones leavened with bicarbonate of soda and baked for breakfast or tea.
instructions: Heat oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and line a tray.
Mix flours, bicarbonate of soda and salt. Rub butter in until crumbly.
Make a well and stir in buttermilk with a knife until a soft dough forms. Turn onto a lightly floured surface and pat to 2 cm thick.
Cut 8 rounds, place on tray, brush with milk and bake 15–18 minutes until risen and browned. Cool slightly on a rack.
recipes.sides: Serve warm with butter, jam or cheddar.
recipes.substitutions: Use the milk-and-lemon buttermilk substitute described for soda bread. Avoid overworking the dough.
recipes.storage: Best on the day. Freeze once cool and thaw before warming in a low oven.
recipes.safety: Do not taste raw dough; ensure the centre of larger scones is baked through.

recipes.name: Sekeli-style pork and sauerkraut goulash
recipes.region: Transylvania association; popular in Central Europe
recipes.description: A gently paprika-seasoned pork and sauerkraut stew finished with sour cream. Preserved as Bruno's existing household recipe.
ingredients: 600 g pork shoulder, in 2 cm cubes
instructions: Warm oil in a heavy pot. Brown pork in batches and set aside.
Cook onions over medium-low heat until soft. Remove pot from heat, stir in paprika, then add a splash of water so it does not scorch.
Return pork. Add sauerkraut, bay leaf and remaining water. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover and cook about 75 minutes until pork is tender; add water if needed.
Temper sour cream with a few spoonfuls of hot liquid, stir it into the pot and warm gently without boiling. Season after tasting.
recipes.sides: Serve with bread or potato dumplings, as Bruno prefers.
recipes.substitutions: Rinse sauerkraut if it is very sour. Plain yoghurt is less traditional and should be stirred in off the heat.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 3 days. Reheat gently until steaming hot; avoid boiling after adding sour cream.
recipes.safety: Keep raw pork separate and cook until tender and hot throughout.

recipes.name: Apple pancakes
recipes.description: Small griddle pancakes with grated apple folded into a lightly spiced batter.
ingredients: Butter or oil for the pan
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, cinnamon and sugar. Whisk egg with milk and stir into dry ingredients until just combined.
Squeeze excess juice from grated apple and fold it into the batter.
Heat a lightly greased pan over medium-low heat. Spoon in small rounds and cook until bubbles form and edges look set, about 2 minutes.
Flip and cook 1–2 minutes until golden and cooked through. Repeat with remaining batter.
recipes.sides: Serve warm with butter, honey or stewed fruit.
recipes.substitutions: Use pear instead of apple or omit cinnamon. Add a spoonful of oats for a coarser texture.
recipes.storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat in a pan until hot.
recipes.safety: Cook through the centre, especially if making larger pancakes.

recipes.name: Bacon potato cakes
recipes.description: Leftover mashed potato mixed with bacon and herbs, shaped and pan-fried for a quick meal.
instructions: Mix cold mash with bacon, spring onion, pepper and enough flour to make a shapeable mixture.
Divide into 8 portions and pat into 1.5 cm thick cakes. Dust lightly with flour.
Heat oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook cakes in batches for 4 minutes per side until crisp and piping hot in the centre.
Drain briefly and serve while hot.
recipes.sides: Serve with fried eggs, baked beans or a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use cooked ham or grated cheddar instead of bacon. If mash contains lots of butter or milk, add a little more flour.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 2 days. Reheat in a pan until hot all the way through.
recipes.safety: Use only properly chilled leftover mash and bacon. Do not leave cooked leftovers at room temperature for long periods.

recipes.name: Sausages with onion gravy
recipes.description: Pan-cooked sausages served with a simple onion gravy and mashed potatoes for a familiar weeknight dinner.
ingredients: 500 ml low-salt beef or chicken stock
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and cook sausages over medium-low heat, turning frequently for 15–18 minutes until browned and cooked through. Transfer to a plate.
Add onions to the pan and cook gently for 10 minutes until soft and golden, stirring often.
Stir in flour for one minute. Gradually add stock while stirring, then simmer 5 minutes until gravy thickens.
Stir in mustard and pepper, return sausages to the pan and simmer 3 minutes. Check sausages are piping hot before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve with champ, mashed potato or boiled potatoes and peas.
recipes.substitutions: Use vegetarian sausages with vegetable stock. A teaspoon of Worcestershire sauce is optional.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Cook pork sausages through to the centre. Keep utensils used for raw sausage separate from cooked food.

recipes.name: Irish boxty potato cakes
recipes.description: Pan-fried potato cakes combining grated raw potato with cooked mash.
instructions: Coarsely grate raw potatoes and squeeze out excess liquid using a clean tea towel.
Mix grated potato with mash, flour, baking powder, egg and seasoning. Add milk gradually until a thick batter holds together.
Heat a little butter or oil in a frying pan over medium-low heat. Spoon in rounds and flatten gently.
Fry 4–5 minutes per side until browned and cooked through. Lower heat if outside browns before centre is done.
recipes.sides: Serve with butter, eggs or a savoury meal.
recipes.substitutions: Use leftover mash; if mixture is loose, add flour a tablespoon at a time.
recipes.storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days and reheat in a pan until hot.
recipes.safety: Cook grated potato mixture promptly because it discolours; ensure cakes are hot through the centre.

recipes.name: Sausage and root vegetable pot
recipes.description: A simple oven-braised pot of sausages, carrots and potatoes for a family supper.
instructions: Heat oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Brown sausages in oil in a frying pan, turning for 6 minutes, then set aside.
Layer onion, carrots and potatoes in an ovenproof casserole. Sprinkle with thyme and pepper.
Set sausages on top and pour in stock. Cover and bake 50 minutes.
Uncover and bake 15–20 minutes until potatoes are tender and sausages are fully cooked. Add hot stock if the pot is drying before potatoes soften.
recipes.sides: Serve with cabbage or peas and mustard.
recipes.substitutions: Use chicken sausages and matching stock; add parsnip in winter.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 3 days. Reheat covered until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Brown sausages are not necessarily cooked through; finish them in the oven and check the centre.

recipes.name: Mushroom and barley soup
recipes.description: A nourishing soup of mushrooms, barley and vegetables, suitable for a simple lunch.
instructions: Rinse barley under cold water. Heat oil in a pot and cook onion and carrot for 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms and thyme; cook 5 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid.
Stir in barley and stock. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 35–40 minutes until barley is tender, adding water if the soup becomes too thick.
Season with pepper and parsley. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve with brown bread or oatcakes.
recipes.substitutions: Use chopped celery in place of carrot. Check the barley packet for cooking time and liquid needs.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate up to 3 days. Barley absorbs broth, so add water when reheating; heat until steaming.
recipes.safety: Rinse barley and keep the soup refrigerated once cooled; do not leave cooked grains at room temperature.

recipes.name: Baked apples with oats
recipes.description: Whole apples baked with oats, brown sugar and butter until soft, an easy home pudding.
instructions: Heat oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Core apples without cutting through the base and place in a small baking dish.
Mix oats, sugar, butter and cinnamon. Pack mixture into the apple centres.
Pour water around the apples and bake 30–35 minutes, basting once, until a knife slides into the flesh easily.
Rest 5 minutes before serving; spoon pan juices over the apples.
recipes.sides: Serve warm with custard, cream or yoghurt.
recipes.substitutions: Use raisins in the filling or replace cinnamon with mixed spice. Reduce sugar for sweet apples.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat gently until hot.
recipes.safety: The filling and fruit become very hot; let them cool slightly before serving.

recipes.name: Mashed turnip
recipes.description: Soft swede mashed with butter and pepper, a common winter side for meat and potato meals.
ingredients: 800 g swede (rutabaga), peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
instructions: Put swede in a pot and cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt, bring to a boil and simmer 20–25 minutes until very tender.
Drain thoroughly and return swede to the warm pot for a minute to evaporate surface moisture.
Mash with butter and pepper. Add milk a teaspoon at a time only if needed for a softer texture.
Taste, season and serve hot.
recipes.sides: Serve with bacon and cabbage, sausages or roast meat.
recipes.substitutions: Carrot may be mashed with swede for a sweeter side. In Ireland the names turnip and swede vary by region; this recipe uses swede.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 3 days. Reheat covered with a splash of water until hot.
recipes.safety: Use a stable chopping board and a sharp knife for the firm raw swede; cut carefully.

recipes.name: Savoury mince with potatoes
recipes.description: A practical minced beef and vegetable stew served over potatoes, common in home cooking.
instructions: Heat oil in a saucepan. Add beef and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains and the liquid has mostly evaporated.
Add onion and carrots; cook 6 minutes until beginning to soften. Stir in flour and tomato paste for one minute.
Gradually pour in stock while stirring. Add Worcestershire sauce, bring to a simmer and cook uncovered 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in peas for the last 4 minutes. Season and serve when the carrots are tender and the sauce has thickened.
recipes.sides: Serve with boiled potatoes, champ or mashed potato.
recipes.substitutions: Use minced lamb or a plant-based mince; adjust cooking time and stock according to its package.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat until bubbling and steaming throughout.
recipes.safety: Cook minced beef thoroughly and avoid cross-contamination from raw meat or utensils.

recipes.name: Haddock in parsley sauce
recipes.description: Flaky haddock served with a simple white parsley sauce and boiled potatoes.
ingredients: 4 skinless haddock fillets, about 150 g each
instructions: Put haddock in a shallow pan with milk and bay leaf. Cover and poach gently 8–10 minutes until fish is opaque and flakes easily. Lift fish to warm plates.
Melt butter in a small saucepan. Stir in flour and cook for one minute.
Strain poaching milk gradually into the flour mixture, whisking until smooth. Simmer 3–4 minutes until thickened.
Stir in parsley, lemon juice and pepper. Spoon sauce over fish and serve.
recipes.sides: Serve with boiled potatoes and peas.
recipes.substitutions: Use cod or hake. If using smoked haddock, taste before adding salt.
recipes.storage: Best served fresh. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 1 day; reheat fish gently until hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw fish chilled and separate. Cook until opaque and easily flaked.

recipes.name: Buttered cabbage
recipes.description: Tender cabbage gently cooked with butter, served as an everyday side with potatoes or bacon.
ingredients: 1 small green cabbage, cored and shredded
instructions: Rinse shredded cabbage and shake off excess water. Melt butter in a wide saucepan over medium-low heat.
Add cabbage and water, cover and cook 8 minutes, turning once or twice.
Uncover and cook another 2–4 minutes until tender and the excess water has evaporated.
Season with pepper and salt to taste. Serve promptly.
recipes.sides: Serve with bacon, ham, sausages or boiled potatoes.
recipes.substitutions: Use savoy cabbage or spring greens; reduce cooking time for tender greens.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 2 days. Reheat once in a pan until hot.
recipes.safety: Avoid overcooking; drain excess liquid before serving to keep the dish from becoming watery.

recipes.name: Cauliflower soup
recipes.description: A mild, creamy soup of cauliflower and potato, blended until smooth for a simple lunch.
instructions: Melt butter in a saucepan and soften onion for 5 minutes.
Add cauliflower, potato and stock. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook 15–18 minutes until vegetables are soft.
Blend carefully in batches until smooth. Return to the pan, stir in milk and heat gently without boiling.
Season with pepper and top with chives.
recipes.sides: Serve with wheaten bread or a cheese toastie.
recipes.substitutions: Use cream instead of milk for a richer soup, or omit dairy and add stock. A little grated cheddar can be stirred in off the heat.
recipes.storage: Cool quickly, refrigerate up to 3 days and reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Vent a blender when processing hot soup. Cool leftovers promptly before refrigeration.

recipes.name: Baked potatoes with cheddar
recipes.description: Crisp-skinned potatoes baked until fluffy and topped with mature Irish cheddar.
ingredients: 4 large floury baking potatoes, about 250 g each
4 tbsp plain yoghurt or sour cream
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Scrub potatoes and dry well. Prick each several times with a fork, rub lightly with oil and salt.
Place directly on an oven rack with a tray below and bake 60–70 minutes until skins are crisp and centres yield easily.
Split potatoes lengthwise and fluff the inside with a fork. Add cheddar while hot so it melts.
Top with yoghurt or sour cream and spring onions. Serve immediately.
recipes.sides: Serve with a green salad, baked beans or leftover chilli.
recipes.substitutions: Use butter instead of yoghurt, or add cooked bacon and chives. Choose floury potatoes for a fluffy centre.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 2 days. Reheat until piping hot; do not leave foil-wrapped potatoes at room temperature.
recipes.safety: Do not wrap potatoes in foil for prolonged room-temperature holding; cool and refrigerate leftovers promptly.

recipes.name: Buttered carrots
recipes.description: Sweet carrots boiled until just tender and tossed in butter and parsley, a simple everyday side.
instructions: Put carrots in a saucepan and cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt and bring to a boil.
Simmer 10–15 minutes depending on thickness until tender but not mushy. Drain well.
Return carrots to the warm pan with butter and parsley. Toss until butter melts.
Season with pepper and serve hot.
recipes.sides: Serve with roast meat, bacon and cabbage or a vegetable pie.
recipes.substitutions: Use a teaspoon of rapeseed oil for a dairy-free version. Add a little lemon zest for brightness.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 3 days. Reheat in a covered pan with a splash of water.
recipes.safety: Cut carrots into even pieces so they cook at a similar rate.

recipes.name: Tomato and red lentil soup
recipes.description: A practical pantry soup of red lentils, tomatoes and vegetables; a modern everyday dish rather than an old regional specialty.
instructions: Warm oil in a saucepan. Cook onion and carrot for 6–8 minutes until soft. Stir in garlic and cumin for 30 seconds.
Add rinsed lentils, tomatoes and stock. Bring to a boil, then lower heat and simmer uncovered for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lentils are soft.
Blend part or all of the soup, taking care with hot liquid, or leave it chunky. Add water if you prefer it thinner.
Season with black pepper and lemon juice to taste.
recipes.sides: Serve with bread and a spoon of plain yoghurt.
recipes.substitutions: Add chopped spinach for the final few minutes. Use less cumin for a milder soup.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate and use within 3 days. Reheat until bubbling and steaming throughout.
recipes.safety: Rinse lentils and follow the package directions; blend hot soup in small batches with the lid vented.

recipes.name: Alfajores de maicena
recipes.englishName: Cornstarch alfajores with dulce de leche
recipes.description: Tender cornstarch sandwich biscuits filled with dulce de leche and rolled in coconut.
instructions: Heat oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Whisk cornstarch, flour and baking powder. Cream butter and sugar; beat in yolks, vanilla and zest.
Fold dry ingredients into butter mixture until a soft dough forms. Chill 20 minutes, then roll to 6 mm and cut 4 cm rounds.
Bake on a lined tray for 8–10 minutes; the biscuits should remain pale. Cool fully on the tray.
Sandwich pairs with dulce de leche and roll the exposed filling in coconut.
recipes.sides: Serve with coffee or mate.
recipes.substitutions: Use thick milk caramel sold as dulce de leche; ordinary caramel sauce is too runny. Lemon zest can be omitted.
recipes.storage: Keep filled biscuits airtight in a cool place for up to 4 days.
recipes.safety: Cool biscuits completely before filling; hot trays and melted sugar filling can burn.

recipes.name: Asado de tira on the grill
recipes.description: Beef short ribs cooked slowly over steady charcoal heat and seasoned simply with salt.
instructions: Prepare a charcoal grill with a moderate coal bed and a cooler area. Pat ribs dry and salt both sides.
Set ribs bone-side down over indirect or low heat. Cook slowly for about 60 minutes, turning once if the heat is uneven.
Move over hotter coals and grill 5–8 minutes per side to brown. Check thick pieces reach a safe temperature and rest 10 minutes.
Cut between bones and serve with lemon and chimichurri.
recipes.sides: Serve with grilled vegetables, bread and a simple tomato salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use thick beef short ribs suitable for grilling; timing varies with cut thickness and grill heat.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat covered until hot throughout.
recipes.safety: Keep raw beef separate from ready-to-eat foods. Use a clean plate for cooked meat and verify doneness with a thermometer.

recipes.name: Bife a caballo
recipes.description: A simple steakhouse plate of pan-seared beef finished with fried eggs.
instructions: Take steaks from the refrigerator 15 minutes before cooking and pat dry. Heat a heavy pan until very hot.
Rub steaks lightly with oil and season. Sear 2–4 minutes per side depending on thickness and preferred doneness; use a thermometer for safety and rest 5 minutes.
In a second pan melt butter and fry eggs until whites are set. Season lightly.
Place one egg on each steak and serve immediately.
recipes.sides: Common accompaniments are fries, mashed potato or a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use a thick sirloin or rump steak. Cook eggs fully if serving to someone at higher risk from foodborne illness.
recipes.storage: Best freshly cooked. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 3 days.
recipes.safety: Prevent raw-meat juices from contacting cooked food. Use a clean pan or wash it before cooking eggs.

recipes.name: Carbonada criolla
recipes.englishName: Argentine beef, squash and corn stew
recipes.description: A sweet-savory criollo stew combining beef, pumpkin, potato and corn; versions vary by province.
instructions: Brown beef in batches in a heavy pot with oil. Add onion and pepper and cook 6 minutes.
Stir in paprika and tomatoes. Add stock, cover and simmer 45 minutes until beef begins to soften.
Add pumpkin, potatoes and corn. Simmer uncovered 25–30 minutes until vegetables are tender and broth thickens.
Fold in peach if using for a sweet seasonal version. Season and simmer 3 minutes before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve in deep bowls with crusty bread.
recipes.substitutions: Use squash or sweet potato for pumpkin. Fruit is optional and regional; omit it for a less sweet stew.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat until bubbling throughout.
recipes.safety: Brown beef thoroughly and keep raw-meat equipment separate. Cut corn rounds carefully on a stable board.

recipes.name: Chipa guazú
recipes.description: A moist baked corn casserole with onion, eggs and cheese, common in the northeast and shared with neighbouring Paraguay.
instructions: Heat oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Butter a 20 cm baking dish.
Cook onion in butter over medium-low heat for 8 minutes until soft; cool slightly.
Pulse corn briefly in a blender so some kernels remain whole. Mix with onion, eggs, milk, cheese, salt and pepper.
Pour into the dish and bake 40–45 minutes until set in the middle and golden at the edges. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.
recipes.sides: Serve warm with salad or grilled meat.
recipes.substitutions: Use thawed frozen corn if fresh is unavailable; drain it well. A mild cheddar can replace local semi-hard cheese.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat portions until hot throughout.
recipes.safety: Ensure eggs are fully set in the centre; cool leftovers promptly.

recipes.name: Choripán
recipes.description: Grilled chorizo tucked into crusty bread and topped with chimichurri or salsa criolla.
instructions: Prepare a medium grill with a cooler zone. Grill sausages slowly, turning often, for 12–16 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Mix vinegar, parsley, garlic, olive oil and pepper for a quick herb dressing, or use prepared chimichurri.
Split rolls and warm them briefly on the grill.
Place a sausage in each roll, split lengthwise if large, and spoon over the dressing.
recipes.sides: Serve with tomato-onion salsa, grilled peppers or a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use fresh pork sausages with a little paprika if Argentine chorizo is unavailable; avoid cured Spanish chorizo for grilling.
recipes.storage: Cook and serve promptly. Refrigerate cooked sausage within 2 hours and use within 3 days.
recipes.safety: Cook fresh sausage fully to the centre; keep raw sausage and its plate separate from the finished rolls.

recipes.name: Empanadas salteñas
recipes.description: Small baked empanadas filled with hand-cut beef, potato, onion, egg and scallion.
ingredients: 500 g beef skirt or chuck, finely diced by hand
instructions: Cook potato in boiling water for 4 minutes, drain. Soften onions in fat for 8 minutes; stir in beef and cook until no longer pink.
Add potato, paprika, cumin, salt and pepper. Cook 4 minutes, then cool completely. Fold in spring onion and egg; chill filling.
Heat oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Add a spoonful of filling to each pastry round, dampen edges, fold and seal with a firm crimp.
Bake on a hot tray 12–18 minutes until browned and piping hot inside. Rest 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve with a small dish of llajua or a fresh tomato salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use minced beef if hand-cut beef is impractical; keep pieces small. Regional fillings and spice levels vary.
recipes.storage: Chill unbaked empanadas promptly or freeze. Bake from chilled; reheat cooked ones until hot throughout.
recipes.safety: Cool cooked filling before assembling and refrigerate it while working. Cook beef thoroughly.

recipes.name: Empanadas tucumanas
recipes.description: Juicy beef empanadas with onion, scallion and egg, baked or traditionally fried depending on the household.
instructions: Cook onions in oil over medium-low heat for 8 minutes. Add beef and cook, stirring, until browned and no pink remains.
Season with paprika, cumin, salt and pepper. Remove from heat, stir in spring onion and cool completely; fold in chopped egg.
Heat oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Fill pastry rounds, moisten edges, fold and crimp tightly so juices stay inside.
Bake 15–20 minutes until golden. Let stand 5 minutes before eating because the filling is very hot.
recipes.sides: Serve with lemon wedges or a fresh tomato and onion salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use a little diced potato for a heartier filling. Tucumán fillings and cooking methods vary; this is a home baked version.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate cooked empanadas within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat in an oven until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Cool filling before assembly and avoid overfilling. Cook beef thoroughly and keep raw dough separate from ready-to-eat food.

recipes.name: Empanadas de humita
recipes.description: Baked pastry turnovers filled with a thick corn, onion and cheese mixture.
instructions: Melt butter and soften onion for 7 minutes. Stir in corn and cook 5 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over the mixture, stir, then add milk gradually. Simmer until thick enough to hold its shape; stir in cheese, paprika and pepper.
Cool the filling completely. Heat oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Spoon filling onto pastry rounds, fold and crimp firmly.
Bake 15–20 minutes until pastry is golden and filling is hot. Rest briefly before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve with a crisp salad or a mild tomato salsa.
recipes.substitutions: Use thawed frozen corn, drained well. Replace cheese with a firm local cheese that melts without becoming watery.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate filling promptly and use within 2 days. Bake assembled empanadas from chilled and serve hot.
recipes.safety: Cool filling before assembly; hot corn mixture can burn. Do not leave dairy filling at room temperature.

recipes.name: Fainá
recipes.description: A thin chickpea-flour bake commonly eaten alongside a slice of Argentine pizza.
instructions: Whisk chickpea flour, water and salt until smooth. Rest batter for at least 30 minutes so the flour hydrates.
Heat oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Pour oil into a 30 cm metal pan and warm it in the oven until hot but not smoking.
Whisk batter again, pour carefully into the hot pan and bake 20–25 minutes until set and browned at the edges.
Season with pepper and oregano. Cut into wedges and serve hot.
recipes.sides: Traditionally served with or over a slice of mozzarella pizza.
recipes.substitutions: Use water gradually; chickpea flour brands absorb differently. Omit oregano for a plain version.
recipes.storage: Best hot. Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days and re-crisp in a hot oven.
recipes.safety: Handle the preheated pan carefully and set it on a stable heatproof surface.

recipes.name: Fugazzeta
recipes.description: A tall pizza style with mozzarella between two layers of dough and plenty of onion on top.
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt. Add water and olive oil; knead 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and rise about 1 hour until doubled.
Heat oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Oil a 30 cm pan. Divide dough in two and press one piece into the pan.
Scatter mozzarella over the base, leaving a 1 cm border. Cover with the second dough round and pinch edges closed. Spread onion on top and season with oregano and pepper.
Bake 20–25 minutes until the base is cooked and the top onion is soft and lightly browned. Rest 5 minutes before slicing.
recipes.sides: Serve with a green salad or a slice of fainá.
recipes.substitutions: Use low-moisture mozzarella to prevent a soggy centre. Add a little grated parmesan, but keep onion and cheese central.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat in an oven or skillet until hot.
recipes.safety: Let molten cheese cool slightly before serving; the centre stays very hot.

recipes.name: Guiso carrero
recipes.description: A one-pot country-style stew of beef, vegetables and short pasta in a tomato broth.
instructions: Brown beef in batches in a large pot with oil. Add onion, pepper and carrots; cook 7 minutes.
Stir in paprika and tomatoes. Add stock, bring to a simmer and cook covered for 35 minutes until beef is nearly tender.
Stir in pasta and simmer uncovered for the packet time, usually 8–12 minutes, stirring often so it does not stick.
Check beef and pasta are tender, add hot water if the stew is too thick, season and serve.
recipes.sides: Serve with bread and chopped parsley.
recipes.substitutions: Use potatoes instead of pasta, adding them with the stock and allowing extra time. Choose a short pasta that holds its shape.
recipes.storage: Pasta absorbs liquid as it stands. Refrigerate promptly and use within 3 days; add stock when reheating and heat thoroughly.
recipes.safety: Brown beef thoroughly and keep raw-meat equipment separate. Cool cooked pasta dishes promptly.

recipes.name: Guiso de lentejas
recipes.description: A hearty lentil stew with vegetables and optional chorizo, especially welcome in cool weather.
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot. If using chorizo, cook 4 minutes to release its fat; add onion, carrot and pepper and soften for 7 minutes.
Stir in paprika and tomatoes. Add lentils, stock and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered for 35–45 minutes until lentils are tender.
Stir occasionally and add water if the pot gets dry before lentils soften. Remove bay leaf and season after tasting.
Rest 5 minutes so the stew thickens, then serve.
recipes.sides: Serve with crusty bread and a simple salad.
recipes.substitutions: Omit chorizo for a meat-free stew; add diced pumpkin or potato. Follow the lentil packet if it calls for soaking.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze. Reheat until bubbling throughout.
recipes.safety: Rinse lentils and cook until tender. If adding sausage, cook it thoroughly and keep it separate while raw.

recipes.name: Humita en olla
recipes.description: Fresh corn grated or pulsed with onion, squash, milk and cheese into a soft spoonable dish.
instructions: Pulse half the corn briefly; leave the rest whole. Heat butter in a saucepan and soften onion for 7 minutes.
Add corn, pumpkin, milk and paprika. Cook over low heat, stirring often, for 20–25 minutes until thick and the vegetables are tender.
Stir in cheese until it melts. Add a splash of water if the mixture becomes too thick.
Season lightly and serve in bowls while hot.
recipes.sides: Serve with bread or alongside grilled meat; it can also be a light meal by itself.
recipes.substitutions: Use thawed frozen corn and grated butternut squash. A melting semi-hard cheese works well.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat gently, stirring, until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Stir frequently over low heat because corn and milk can catch on the pan bottom.

recipes.name: Humita en chala
recipes.description: A seasoned fresh-corn and cheese mixture wrapped in corn husks and gently steamed.
ingredients: 6 large corn cobs with intact husks
700 g corn kernels, grated or pulsed
instructions: Carefully remove husks from cobs, keeping them whole. Soak husks in warm water for 20 minutes, then drain. Cut kernels from cobs and pulse to a coarse paste.
Cook onion in oil until soft. Mix with corn, cheese, paprika, cumin, salt and pepper.
Overlap two husks in a cross. Add a mound of filling, fold into a packet and tie with a narrow strip of husk or kitchen string.
Steam parcels over simmering water for 40–50 minutes until firm and hot through. Let cool briefly before unwrapping at the table.
recipes.sides: Serve as a main with tomato salad or as part of a northern Argentine meal.
recipes.substitutions: If fresh husks are not available, bake the corn mixture covered in a dish; that is a different presentation, humita en olla.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate cooked parcels promptly and use within 2 days. Reheat by steaming until hot throughout.
recipes.safety: Use only food-safe husks, rinse them well and ensure parcels remain above the simmering water rather than submerged.

recipes.name: Locro criollo
recipes.description: A slow-cooked stew of white corn, beans, squash and pork or beef; many family and provincial versions exist.
ingredients: 250 g dried white hominy corn, soaked overnight
150 g dried white beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Drain soaked corn and beans. Put them in a large pot with beef, pork, bacon, onion and water. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently for 2 hours.
Stir every 15 minutes, scraping the bottom. Add hot water as needed to keep ingredients covered.
Add pumpkin and cook 45–60 minutes more until grains, beans and meat are tender and the pumpkin thickens the broth.
Mash some pumpkin against the pot to thicken. Season and serve with a small spoon of spicy oil or salsa on the side.
recipes.sides: Serve with bread and quiquirimichi or another chilli oil offered separately.
recipes.substitutions: Use dried hominy sold for locro; ordinary sweetcorn will not give the same texture. Meat choices vary; omit pork and increase beans for a different version.
recipes.storage: Cool quickly, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze. Reheat to a full simmer, stirring often.
recipes.safety: Soak dried beans and corn in the refrigerator if the room is warm; discard soaking water and cook thoroughly. Keep stew hot or cool it promptly.

recipes.name: Milanesa de carne
recipes.description: Thin beef cutlets coated in seasoned crumbs and fried until crisp, a familiar home and bodegón meal.
ingredients: 600 g thin beef top round steaks
instructions: Pound steaks evenly to about 5 mm. Season flour with salt and pepper. Beat eggs with milk, garlic and parsley.
Coat each steak in flour, dip in egg, then press into breadcrumbs. Chill 10 minutes so the coating adheres.
Heat 1 cm oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry cutlets in batches 2–3 minutes per side until golden and beef is cooked through.
Drain on a rack and serve hot with lemon.
recipes.sides: Serve with mashed potatoes, fries, or tomato and lettuce salad.
recipes.substitutions: Chicken breast can be used for a milanesa de pollo; flatten it evenly and cook fully through.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate cooked cutlets within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Re-crisp in a hot oven.
recipes.safety: Keep raw beef separate from crumbs and cooked food. Use fresh crumbs for each batch and cook cutlets thoroughly.

recipes.name: Milanesa a la napolitana
recipes.englishName: Beef cutlet with tomato and cheese
recipes.description: A breaded beef cutlet topped with tomato sauce, ham and melted cheese; an Argentine bodegón favourite.
ingredients: 4 thin beef cutlets, about 150 g each
instructions: Heat oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Season cutlets. Dip in flour, beaten egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing crumbs on firmly.
Shallow-fry cutlets in batches 2–3 minutes per side until golden and beef is cooked; drain on a rack.
Place on a baking tray. Top each with a spoon of passata, ham, mozzarella and oregano.
Bake 6–8 minutes until cheese melts and bubbles. Serve hot.
recipes.sides: Serve with fries, mashed potatoes or a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use chicken cutlets for a chicken version. Use cooked tomato sauce that is thick enough not to soak the crust.
recipes.storage: Best served straight away. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 2 days; reheat in an oven until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Cook beef fully before topping. Avoid cross-contamination between raw cutlets and cheese or cooked sauce.

recipes.name: Ñoquis de papa
recipes.description: Soft potato dumplings, often eaten on the 29th of the month with a simple tomato sauce.
instructions: Boil whole potatoes with skins until tender, 25–35 minutes. Drain, peel while warm and pass through a ricer; let steam escape until dry.
Mix potato with egg and salt. Fold in flour just until a soft dough forms; do not knead heavily.
Roll portions into ropes about 1.5 cm thick, cut into 2 cm pieces and press lightly with a fork. Cook in batches in salted boiling water; lift out when they float, about 2 minutes.
Warm passata with oil and garlic for 12 minutes. Toss gnocchi with sauce and cheese.
recipes.sides: Serve with grated hard cheese and a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use a plain tomato sauce or tuco with meat. Add flour sparingly; too much makes gnocchi heavy.
recipes.storage: Shape and freeze uncooked gnocchi on a tray, then bag. Cook from frozen; refrigerate leftovers and use within 2 days.
recipes.safety: Let potatoes cool enough to handle. Cook gnocchi until they float and are hot through.

recipes.name: Pastel de papa
recipes.description: Seasoned minced beef with onion, olives and egg baked under a mashed-potato crust.
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil potatoes until tender, drain and mash with butter and milk.
Brown beef in oil, breaking it up. Add onions and cook 7 minutes. Stir in paprika, cumin and pepper; cook until beef is fully browned.
Remove from heat and fold in olives and chopped egg. Spread filling in a baking dish and cover evenly with mash; roughen with a fork.
Bake 25–30 minutes until the top is golden and the centre is piping hot. Rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve with a tomato, lettuce and onion salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use raisins in a small portion for a sweet-savory family variation, or omit olives and egg if preferred.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 3 days. Reheat portions until steaming hot throughout.
recipes.safety: Cook minced beef thoroughly and cool leftovers quickly before refrigeration.

recipes.name: Pastelitos criollos
recipes.englishName: Fried quince or sweet potato pastries
recipes.description: Crisp layered pastries filled with quince paste or sweet potato paste, traditionally served around national holidays.
ingredients: 200 g quince paste or sweet potato paste
100 g sugar syrup or honey, optional
instructions: Mix flour and salt. Rub in butter, add water gradually and knead 5 minutes to a smooth dough. Cover and rest 20 minutes.
Roll dough thinly, brush with oil and fold in thirds. Turn, roll again and repeat once. Rest 10 minutes, then roll to 3 mm and cut 24 squares.
Put a small cube of paste in the centre of 12 squares. Brush edges with water, cover with remaining squares at an angle and press around filling.
Fry in 170°C oil in small batches, spooning hot oil over tops to help layers puff. Drain and brush with syrup if using.
recipes.sides: Serve warm with mate or tea.
recipes.substitutions: Use firm quince paste or dulce de batata. If you do not have a thermometer, test oil with a small dough scrap; it should bubble steadily, not burn quickly.
recipes.storage: Best on the day. Keep cooled pastries loosely covered for 1 day; re-crisp briefly in an oven.
recipes.safety: Hot oil can ignite or splatter. Use a deep stable pot, fry small batches and never leave oil unattended.

recipes.name: Pollo al disco
recipes.description: Chicken and vegetables slowly braised outdoors in a wide plow-disc pan; this home version uses a heavy skillet.
ingredients: 250 ml dry white wine or stock
instructions: Heat a wide heavy pan over medium-high heat. Brown chicken pieces in oil in batches; set aside.
Cook onions, pepper and carrots in the same pan for 8 minutes. Stir in paprika and oregano.
Return chicken with tomatoes and wine or stock. Bring to a simmer, cover loosely and cook 35–40 minutes, turning chicken once, until tender.
Uncover for 5 minutes to reduce sauce. Check the thickest chicken piece reaches 75°C; season and serve.
recipes.sides: Serve with bread, rice or potatoes to absorb the sauce.
recipes.substitutions: Use stock in place of wine. Add peas or sliced potatoes for a fuller one-pot meal.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 3 days. Reheat until bubbling and steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw chicken separate and cook to 75°C at the thickest part. Wash hands and utensils after handling.

recipes.name: Provoleta a la parrilla
recipes.description: A thick slice of provolone grilled until browned outside and molten within, seasoned with oregano.
ingredients: 400 g provolone, cut into 2 cm rounds
instructions: Heat a grill to medium-high and place a small cast-iron dish or heatproof skillet over the coals to warm.
Set provolone in the dish and grill 3–4 minutes until the underside browns and edges soften.
Turn carefully with a wide spatula and cook another 2–3 minutes until bubbling.
Sprinkle with oregano, chilli if using, and pepper. Serve immediately with bread.
recipes.sides: Serve as a shared starter before asado, with bread and grilled vegetables.
recipes.substitutions: Use a firm grilling cheese that softens without running away; ordinary soft mozzarella is not suitable.
recipes.storage: Serve hot; melted cheese firms as it cools and is best not stored.
