recipes.safety: Use heatproof gloves and a stable dish; melted cheese and the pan are extremely hot.

recipes.name: Matambre arrollado
recipes.description: Thin flank steak rolled around vegetables and hard-boiled egg, then gently cooked and chilled for slices.
instructions: Lay steak flat and trim thick hard fat. Season with salt, pepper, garlic, parsley and oregano.
Arrange carrot, pepper and peeled eggs along one long edge. Roll tightly with the grain, tucking filling in as you go; tie securely every 3 cm.
Put roll in a pot, cover with water, bring to a simmer and cook gently 90–100 minutes until tender and fully cooked.
Drain, press under a clean weight while cooling, then chill completely. Remove string and slice across the roll.
recipes.sides: Serve cold with potato salad, salsa criolla or a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use spinach or cooked peas in place of pepper. Filling combinations vary by household.
recipes.storage: Keep covered and refrigerated; use within 3 days. Usually served cold, so do not leave it out for long.
recipes.safety: Tie with clean food-safe string, cook beef thoroughly and chill promptly. Keep raw steak away from the cooked filling ingredients.

recipes.name: Matambre a la pizza
recipes.englishName: Flank steak with tomato and cheese
recipes.description: Tenderised flank steak topped with tomato, oregano and melted cheese, finished under a hot grill.
instructions: Trim steak and place in a shallow dish. Cover with milk, garlic and oregano; refrigerate 2–4 hours to tenderise, then drain and pat dry.
Heat oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Place steak in an oiled baking dish, season and cover tightly with foil.
Bake 35–45 minutes until tender. Remove foil, spoon over passata and scatter mozzarella.
Return to oven or grill for 8–10 minutes until cheese melts and browns lightly. Rest 5 minutes and slice across the grain.
recipes.sides: Serve with fries or a crisp salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use a lean flank or skirt cut. The milk marinade is optional for a naturally tender cut; refrigerate during marinating.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat until hot throughout.
recipes.safety: Discard used marinade. Cook beef to a safe doneness and keep raw-meat utensils separate from toppings.

recipes.name: Sorrentinos de jamón y queso
recipes.description: Large round filled pasta associated with Mar del Plata, served with a simple tomato sauce.
instructions: Make pasta dough by mixing flour, eggs, oil and salt. Knead 8 minutes until smooth; wrap and rest 30 minutes.
Mix ham, mozzarella and ricotta. Roll dough thinly, place teaspoons of filling spaced apart, cover with another sheet and press around each mound to seal. Cut into large rounds.
Warm passata with garlic and oil for 15 minutes. Bring a pot of salted water to a gentle boil.
Cook pasta in batches 4–6 minutes until they float and pasta is tender. Lift with a slotted spoon and serve with sauce.
recipes.sides: Serve with grated hard cheese and salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use cooked chicken with cheese or spinach and ricotta for another filling. Ensure edges are sealed to prevent leaks.
recipes.storage: Freeze uncooked pasta in a single layer, then bag. Cook from frozen for a few extra minutes; refrigerate cooked leftovers up to 2 days.
recipes.safety: Keep fresh pasta chilled if not cooked promptly. Filling should be kept cold during preparation.

recipes.name: Tamales salteños
recipes.description: Cornmeal parcels filled with seasoned beef, wrapped in husks and steamed until firm.
instructions: Cook onion in oil until soft. Add beef, paprika, cumin, salt and pepper; cook until beef is browned. Cool filling.
Stir cornmeal into warm stock with butter and salt. Cook over low heat, stirring, until thick and spoonable, about 8 minutes; cool until handleable.
Spread corn dough on each softened husk, add a spoon of filling, fold sides inward and tie ends with strips of husk.
Steam parcels over simmering water for 60–75 minutes until the dough is firm. Rest 5 minutes before unwrapping.
recipes.sides: Serve hot with salsa and a tomato salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use fresh corn husks or food-safe parchment tied with string. Some regional versions use other meats or raisins.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 2 days. Reheat by steaming until hot through.
recipes.safety: Use clean food-safe husks and keep filling chilled until assembly. Cook beef completely before wrapping.

recipes.name: Tortas fritas
recipes.description: Simple rounds of flour dough fried until puffed and crisp, often eaten on rainy afternoons with mate.
instructions: Mix flour and salt. Rub in lard, then add warm water gradually to form a soft dough.
Knead briefly until smooth, cover and rest 15 minutes. Divide into 8 balls and roll each into a 5 mm round; make a small slit in the centre.
Heat 3 cm oil in a deep pot to about 175°C. Fry one or two rounds at a time, turning once, until puffed and golden on both sides.
Drain on a rack or paper towels. Dust lightly with sugar if desired and serve warm.
recipes.sides: Serve with mate, tea, or a little dulce de leche.
recipes.substitutions: Use vegetable shortening instead of lard. Add water slowly because flour absorption differs.
recipes.storage: Eat the same day; they lose crispness as they cool.
recipes.safety: Hot oil is hazardous. Use a deep stable pot, monitor temperature and never leave it unattended.

recipes.name: Tarta de jamón y queso
recipes.description: A practical everyday tart with ham, cheese and egg custard in a pastry shell.
ingredients: 1 round shortcrust pastry sheet, about 280 g
instructions: Heat oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Line a 24 cm tart tin with pastry, prick the base and chill 10 minutes.
Blind bake with baking paper and weights for 12 minutes; remove weights and bake 5 minutes more.
Scatter ham and cheese in the shell. Whisk eggs, milk, mustard, pepper and parsley; pour over filling.
Bake 25–30 minutes until the centre is just set and lightly golden. Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
recipes.sides: Serve warm or at room temperature with a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use cooked chicken or sautéed vegetables. Choose a firm melting cheese and reduce salt if ham is salty.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat slices until hot or serve chilled.
recipes.safety: Bake egg custard until set in the centre and refrigerate leftovers promptly.

recipes.name: Tarta de acelga
recipes.description: A home-style savoury tart filled with tender chard, onion and egg in a pastry crust.
ingredients: 500 g Swiss chard, washed and chopped
instructions: Heat oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Line a tart tin with pastry, prick the base and blind bake 15 minutes.
Cook chard in a covered pan with its rinsing water for 5 minutes until wilted. Drain and squeeze out excess liquid.
Soften onion in oil for 6 minutes. Mix with chard, 2 beaten eggs, cheese, nutmeg and pepper.
Fill pastry shell. Brush edge with remaining beaten egg and bake 25–30 minutes until set and browned. Rest before cutting.
recipes.sides: Serve with tomato salad; slices are also eaten at room temperature.
recipes.substitutions: Use spinach instead of chard, squeezing it very dry. Add ricotta for a softer filling.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat until hot or serve cold.
recipes.safety: Drain greens well so the egg filling sets. Cook until no liquid egg remains in the middle.

recipes.name: Tortilla a la parrilla
recipes.description: A simple flour-and-water flatbread cooked on a hot griddle or grill, a common rural accompaniment.
instructions: Mix flour and salt. Rub in lard or oil, then add warm water gradually until a soft dough forms.
Knead 5 minutes until smooth, cover and rest 15 minutes.
Divide into 6 balls and roll each to a 5 mm round. Prick lightly with a fork to reduce large bubbles.
Cook on a hot dry griddle or grill 2–3 minutes per side until spotted brown and cooked through.
recipes.sides: Serve with asado, cheese or mate.
recipes.substitutions: Use olive oil instead of lard. Add a little more water if the dough cracks while rolling.
recipes.storage: Best freshly cooked. Wrap leftovers and reheat on a dry pan the next day.
recipes.safety: Use a stable griddle and turn flatbreads with tongs; avoid open flames touching the dough.

recipes.name: Pastel de choclo
recipes.description: A baked corn-topped casserole with a seasoned beef filling, related to regional corn-pie traditions.
instructions: Heat oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Cook onion in oil until soft, add beef and paprika and cook until browned. Fold in egg and olives; spread in a baking dish.
Pulse corn coarsely. Cook in a saucepan with milk and butter over medium-low heat, stirring until thick, about 12 minutes.
Spread corn mixture over beef. Sprinkle sugar lightly across the top if a browned sweet edge is wanted.
Bake 25–30 minutes until bubbling and browned. Rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve with a crisp salad and salsa.
recipes.substitutions: Use diced chicken or omit meat for a vegetable corn bake; regional recipes differ in filling and sweetness.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate up to 3 days and reheat until steaming throughout.
recipes.safety: Cook minced beef fully and ensure the centre of the casserole is piping hot.

recipes.name: Tortilla de papas
recipes.description: A thick potato and onion omelette common in Argentine home cooking and cafés.
ingredients: 600 g potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a non-stick pan. Add potatoes and onion, cover and cook over low heat 15–18 minutes, turning gently, until tender but not browned.
Beat eggs with salt and pepper in a bowl. Fold in cooked potato and onion; rest 5 minutes.
Wipe pan, add remaining oil and pour mixture in. Cook on low 6–8 minutes until edges set and centre is nearly firm.
Slide onto a plate, invert back into pan and cook 3–4 minutes on the other side until fully set. Rest before slicing.
recipes.sides: Serve warm or at room temperature with salad or crusty bread.
recipes.substitutions: Add cooked chorizo or parsley if desired. For a softer centre, shorten final cooking only when eggs are safe for the diners.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Serve cold or reheat until hot.
recipes.safety: Cook egg thoroughly for children, older adults, pregnant people or anyone immunocompromised.

recipes.name: Pizza de muzzarella
recipes.description: A tall, soft-based Buenos Aires pizza with tomato, generous mozzarella and oregano.
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt. Add water and oil, knead 8 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and rise about 1 hour.
Oil a 30 cm deep pan. Press dough into it and let rest 15 minutes. Heat oven to 230°C (210°C fan).
Spread passata thinly over dough and bake 8 minutes. Add mozzarella and oregano; bake another 10–12 minutes until base is cooked and cheese bubbles.
Top with olives if using, rest 5 minutes and cut into squares.
recipes.sides: Serve with fainá and a simple salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use low-moisture mozzarella; drain fresh mozzarella well. Add olives after baking if they are very salty.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat in an oven or covered pan.
recipes.safety: Use cooked passata and bake until the dough centre is fully set.

recipes.name: Flan mixto
recipes.description: Silky baked egg custard with caramel, served with dulce de leche and whipped cream.
instructions: Heat oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Melt caramel sugar in a small pan until amber; immediately pour into a 1 litre mould and swirl to coat the base.
Warm milk until steaming but not boiling. Whisk eggs, sugar and vanilla gently; slowly whisk in milk without creating too much foam.
Strain custard into the mould. Set mould in a roasting pan and pour hot water around it halfway up the sides.
Bake 45–55 minutes until edges are set and centre has a slight wobble. Cool, chill at least 4 hours, then loosen edges and invert.
recipes.sides: Serve with dulce de leche and whipped cream, the mixto pairing.
recipes.substitutions: Use a small amount of orange zest instead of vanilla. Do not replace milk with water; custard texture depends on dairy.
recipes.storage: Keep covered and refrigerated; use within 3 days.
recipes.safety: Use care with molten caramel and hot water bath. Keep custard chilled and do not leave it at room temperature for long.

recipes.name: Pastafrola de membrillo
recipes.description: A buttery shortcrust tart filled with quince paste and finished with a lattice top.
instructions: Heat oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Cream butter and sugar, beat in egg and vanilla. Fold in flour and baking powder to make a soft dough; chill 20 minutes.
Reserve one-third of dough. Press remaining dough into a 24 cm tart tin, covering base and sides evenly.
Warm quince paste with water over low heat, stirring until spreadable. Spread over pastry base.
Roll reserved dough and cut strips. Lay a lattice over filling, brush strips with milk and bake 35–40 minutes until lightly golden. Cool before slicing.
recipes.sides: Serve with tea or mate.
recipes.substitutions: Use dulce de batata (sweet potato paste) or a thick fruit preserve. Add water to paste only a little at a time.
recipes.storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 2 days or refrigerate for up to 5 days.
recipes.safety: Let the hot filling cool slightly before spreading; avoid burns from thick fruit paste.

recipes.name: Polenta con tuco
recipes.description: Creamy cornmeal served with a slow tomato sauce, often enriched with beef or sausage.
instructions: Cook onion in olive oil for 6 minutes. Add beef and brown while breaking it apart. Stir in passata and oregano; simmer 25 minutes.
Bring salted water or stock to a boil. Whisk in polenta gradually to prevent lumps.
Cook according to packet directions, stirring often, until creamy and thick; add hot water if it firms too much.
Spoon polenta into bowls, top with tuco and grated cheese.
recipes.sides: Serve with a green salad and extra cheese.
recipes.substitutions: For meat-free tuco, add mushrooms or lentils. Follow the polenta packet for liquid ratio and cooking time.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate sauce and polenta separately up to 3 days. Reheat with liquid until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Polenta can bubble and spit; use a deep pot and stir carefully. Cook minced beef thoroughly.

recipes.name: Puchero criollo
recipes.description: A family pot of beef, potatoes, pumpkin, cabbage and other vegetables cooked in broth and served in courses or together.
instructions: Put beef, onion, bay and water in a large pot. Bring to a gentle boil, skim, then simmer covered for 75 minutes.
Add carrots and potatoes and simmer 20 minutes. Add pumpkin, cabbage and corn and cook another 20–25 minutes until tender.
Lift meat and vegetables carefully to a platter. Strain broth if desired and season it separately.
Serve broth as a first course or ladle it over meat and vegetables in bowls.
recipes.sides: Serve with salsa criolla, mustard or crusty bread.
recipes.substitutions: Use a mix of suitable stewing beef cuts. Seasonal vegetables vary; add them according to how long they take to cook.
recipes.storage: Cool broth and solids promptly, refrigerate separately and use within 3 days. Reheat until fully steaming.
recipes.safety: Keep raw beef separate and simmer until tender. Cool large pots in shallow containers for faster refrigeration.

recipes.name: Revuelto gramajo
recipes.description: A quick skillet of crisp potato strips, ham and softly set eggs, served in cafés and homes.
ingredients: 400 g potatoes, cut into thin matchsticks
100 g cooked ham, cut into strips
instructions: Rinse potato strips, dry very thoroughly and fry in batches at 175°C until golden and crisp. Drain well.
Warm 1 tbsp oil in a wide pan and heat ham for 1 minute.
Beat eggs lightly with pepper, pour into pan and stir slowly over low heat until softly set but not runny.
Fold in crisp potatoes and parsley and serve immediately.
recipes.sides: Serve with a green salad and bread.
recipes.substitutions: Use leftover thin fries instead of frying potatoes from raw. Add peas if desired.
recipes.storage: Best fresh; potato strips soften quickly once mixed with eggs.
recipes.safety: Dry potatoes completely before frying to limit oil splatter. Cook eggs until safely set.

recipes.name: Ravioles con tuco
recipes.description: Filled pasta served with a long-simmered tomato and beef sauce, an everyday Sunday lunch in many homes.
instructions: Heat oil in a saucepan. Cook onion 6 minutes, add beef and brown thoroughly while breaking up lumps.
Stir in passata, oregano and bay leaf. Simmer gently 30–35 minutes, stirring occasionally; add a little water if it thickens too much.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook ravioli according to package directions. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Remove bay leaf, spoon tuco over ravioli and finish with grated cheese.
recipes.sides: Serve with salad and bread.
recipes.substitutions: Use spinach-ricotta or meat ravioli; check package cooking time. Omit beef for a tomato-only sauce.
recipes.storage: Keep sauce refrigerated up to 3 days. Cook pasta fresh if possible; refrigerate leftovers and use within 2 days.
recipes.safety: Cook minced beef thoroughly. Keep fresh filled pasta refrigerated and follow its use-by instructions.

recipes.name: Tarta de choclo
recipes.description: A savoury pastry tart filled with corn, onion, egg and cheese for lunch or a light supper.
instructions: Heat oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Line a tart tin with pastry and blind bake for 15 minutes.
Cook onion in butter for 6 minutes. Add corn and cook 5 minutes; cool slightly.
Whisk eggs with milk and pepper. Stir in corn mixture and half the cheese; pour into pastry shell and top with remaining cheese.
Bake 25–30 minutes until centre is set and top is golden. Rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve with lettuce and tomato salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use thawed frozen corn, drained. Add diced cooked ham for a non-vegetarian version.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Serve cold or reheat until hot.
recipes.safety: Bake until egg filling is set in the middle. Cool leftovers promptly.

recipes.name: Vitel toné
recipes.description: Chilled sliced veal under a creamy tuna, anchovy and caper sauce, commonly served for summer celebrations.
instructions: Put veal, onion, carrot, celery and bay in a pot with water. Bring to a simmer and cook gently 75–90 minutes until tender and safely cooked.
Cool meat in its broth, then cover and refrigerate until cold. Reserve a little broth.
Blend tuna, anchovies, mayonnaise, half the capers and lemon juice. Add broth by the spoonful until sauce is spoonable; chill.
Slice veal thinly across the grain, arrange on a platter, cover with sauce and garnish with remaining capers.
recipes.sides: Serve cold with bread and a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use lean beef eye round if veal is unavailable. Use Greek yoghurt for part of the mayonnaise, though flavour will be tangier.
recipes.storage: Keep covered and refrigerated; use within 2 days because the sauce contains fish and mayonnaise.
recipes.safety: Cool meat promptly and keep chilled. Do not leave the assembled platter unrefrigerated for extended periods.

recipes.name: Mate cocido
recipes.description: A mild hot infusion of yerba mate brewed in water and strained into cups, often served with breakfast or merienda.
instructions: Heat water in a saucepan until steaming but not at a rolling boil, about 80°C.
Add yerba mate and simmer very gently for 3–4 minutes; avoid vigorous boiling which can make it bitter.
Turn off heat and steep 2 minutes. Strain through a fine sieve into cups.
Serve plain, with milk, or sweeten to taste.
recipes.sides: Serve with toast, facturas or biscuits.
recipes.substitutions: Use a tea infuser for easier straining. Adjust yerba amount and steep time to taste.
recipes.storage: Brew fresh; do not leave the infusion at room temperature for hours.
recipes.safety: Hot drinks can scald; let cool to a comfortable temperature before serving children.

recipes.name: Empanadas de carne cortada a cuchillo
recipes.description: Baked turnovers with finely hand-cut beef, onion, scallion and egg; this filling is kept simple to let the meat stand out.
ingredients: 500 g beef, diced 5 mm by hand
instructions: Cook onion in oil over medium-low heat until soft, 8–10 minutes. Add beef and cook until browned, stirring so pieces cook evenly.
Season with paprika, cumin, salt and pepper. Remove from heat, stir in spring onion and cool completely; fold in egg.
Heat oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Put filling on pastry rounds, moisten edges and crimp tightly.
Bake 12–18 minutes until browned. Rest briefly before eating.
recipes.sides: Serve with llajua, lemon wedges or salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use minced beef if needed, while noting the hand-cut texture is part of this version. Regional empanada fillings differ.
recipes.storage: Chill filling promptly. Refrigerate baked empanadas up to 3 days and reheat until hot.
recipes.safety: Do not leave cooked filling at room temperature while assembling; keep it chilled and cook beef thoroughly.

recipes.name: Budín de pan
recipes.description: A thrifty baked custard pudding made with stale bread, milk, eggs and caramel.
instructions: Heat oven to 170°C (150°C fan). Melt caramel sugar in a small pan until amber and pour into a loaf tin, coating the base.
Warm milk and pour over torn bread. Leave 10 minutes, then mash until mostly smooth.
Whisk eggs, sugar and vanilla; stir into bread mixture with raisins if using. Pour into tin.
Bake in a water bath for 50–60 minutes until set with a slight wobble. Cool, chill, then turn out.
recipes.sides: Serve chilled with dulce de leche or whipped cream.
recipes.substitutions: Use stale rolls or brioche; reduce sugar for sweet bread. Raisins are optional.
recipes.storage: Cover and refrigerate; use within 3 days.
recipes.safety: Use a stable water bath and take care moving hot water. Keep custard chilled after cooling.

recipes.name: Empanadas de jamón y queso
recipes.description: A popular quick filling of cooked ham and melting cheese enclosed in pastry and baked until crisp.
instructions: Heat oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Mix ham, mozzarella, oregano and pepper.
Place a small mound in the centre of each pastry round. Brush edge with water, fold over and press firmly, then crimp or seal with a fork.
Arrange on a lined tray with space between. Brush tops with beaten egg.
Bake 15–18 minutes until golden and cheese is bubbling. Cool 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve with tomato salad or a mild salsa.
recipes.substitutions: Use a firm melting cheese and avoid watery fresh mozzarella. Add a little sautéed onion if desired.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 3 days. Reheat in an oven until hot.
recipes.safety: Cool the filling if preparing ahead and keep assembled pastries chilled until baking.

recipes.name: Pollo al horno con papas
recipes.description: A practical family tray meal of chicken pieces roasted with potatoes, garlic and oregano.
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Put potatoes in a roasting tray, toss with half the oil, salt and pepper.
Rub chicken with remaining oil, garlic, oregano, lemon zest and pepper. Arrange skin-side up among potatoes.
Roast 55–65 minutes, turning potatoes once, until chicken is browned and juices run clear; check thickest part reaches 75°C.
Rest chicken 10 minutes and serve with pan juices.
recipes.sides: Serve with tomato and lettuce salad or chimichurri.
recipes.substitutions: Use bone-in thighs or drumsticks; timings vary with size. Add sliced onion to the tray.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw chicken and its juices separate. Cook to 75°C at the thickest part and wash hands and tools after handling.

recipes.name: Ensalada rusa
recipes.description: Chilled potatoes, carrots and peas folded with mayonnaise, common at family meals and asado tables.
instructions: Boil potatoes and carrots separately in salted water until just tender, 10–15 minutes. Add peas for the last 2 minutes.
Drain vegetables well and spread on a tray to cool quickly. Refrigerate until cold.
Fold cold vegetables with mayonnaise, lemon juice, pepper and parsley. Taste and adjust salt.
Chill at least 30 minutes before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve cold with asado, milanesa or sandwiches.
recipes.substitutions: Use a lighter mayonnaise or plain yoghurt for part of it. Add diced cooked egg if desired.
recipes.storage: Keep refrigerated and use within 2 days. Do not leave the salad in warm conditions.
recipes.safety: Cool cooked vegetables quickly and mix only once cold; mayonnaise salads need refrigeration.

recipes.name: Tarta de zapallo
recipes.description: A savoury pumpkin tart with onion and cheese in a pastry shell for lunch or a light dinner.
instructions: Heat oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Roast pumpkin on a tray for 25 minutes until soft; mash and let excess steam escape.
Line a tart tin with pastry and blind bake for 15 minutes. Cook onion in oil until translucent.
Mix pumpkin, onion, eggs, cheese, nutmeg and pepper. Fill pastry shell and smooth the top.
Bake 25–30 minutes until set and golden. Rest before slicing.
recipes.sides: Serve with a crisp green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use butternut squash for pumpkin. Add cooked corn or spinach, squeezing greens dry first.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat until hot or serve cold.
recipes.safety: Bake until the egg filling is set in the centre. Cool and refrigerate promptly.

recipes.name: Pebete de jamón y queso
recipes.description: A soft oval roll filled with ham and cheese, a familiar bakery and lunch-counter sandwich.
instructions: Slice rolls lengthwise without cutting all the way through. Spread a thin layer of butter on the cut sides.
Layer ham and cheese evenly inside each roll; add lettuce or tomato if using.
Close rolls and serve cold, or toast in a sandwich press until cheese softens.
Cut in half and serve immediately.
recipes.sides: Serve with a small salad, crisps or fruit.
recipes.substitutions: Use another soft oval bread roll and a mild melting cheese. Add mustard if desired.
recipes.storage: Assemble just before eating if adding vegetables. Refrigerate filled sandwiches and eat the same day.
recipes.safety: Keep ham and cheese chilled until assembly and do not leave sandwiches in a warm place.

recipes.name: Arroz con leche
recipes.description: Rice slowly simmered in milk with sugar and citrus peel, served chilled with cinnamon.
instructions: Rinse rice briefly. Put it in a heavy saucepan with milk, lemon peel and cinnamon stick.
Bring slowly to a gentle simmer, stirring often. Cook uncovered 30–35 minutes until rice is tender and mixture creamy.
Stir in sugar and vanilla and cook 5 minutes more, stirring so it does not catch. Remove peel and cinnamon stick.
Spoon into bowls, cool and refrigerate. Dust with cinnamon before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve chilled or just warm, with cinnamon.
recipes.substitutions: Use orange peel instead of lemon. Add a little extra milk when reheating because rice thickens as it cools.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate and use within 3 days.
recipes.safety: Stir frequently to prevent scorching and chill cooked rice pudding promptly.

recipes.name: Empanadas de acelga y queso
recipes.description: Baked pastry filled with cooked chard, onion and cheese for a portable lunch or snack.
instructions: Cook chard in a covered pan with its rinsing water for 5 minutes until wilted. Drain, cool and squeeze very dry; chop finely.
Soften onion in oil for 6 minutes. Mix with chard, ricotta, cheese and pepper.
Heat oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Fill pastry rounds, moisten edges and seal with a crimp.
Brush with egg and bake 15–18 minutes until golden. Rest briefly before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve with tomato salad or salsa criolla.
recipes.substitutions: Spinach can replace chard. Squeeze cooked greens thoroughly to avoid soggy pastry.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate cooked empanadas within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat in the oven.
recipes.safety: Cool filling before assembly and keep dairy filling chilled until baking.

recipes.name: Panqueques con dulce de leche
recipes.description: Thin pancakes spread with milk caramel, rolled and lightly dusted with sugar.
instructions: Whisk flour and salt. Beat eggs with milk, then whisk into flour until smooth; stir in melted butter and rest 10 minutes.
Heat a lightly buttered pan. Pour in a thin layer of batter and swirl; cook about 1 minute until edges lift, flip and cook 30 seconds.
Repeat to make 8 pancakes. Spread each with dulce de leche while warm and roll or fold.
Dust lightly with sugar if desired and serve.
recipes.sides: Serve as dessert with coffee or a little whipped cream.
recipes.substitutions: Use thick milk caramel; loosen a very firm filling with gentle warmth. Do not use runny caramel sauce.
recipes.storage: Best freshly filled. Refrigerate leftovers and use within 2 days.
recipes.safety: Let pancakes cool slightly before filling; hot caramel can burn.

recipes.name: Carbonada en zapallo
recipes.description: A celebratory presentation of carbonada served inside a baked squash; the filling is a regional sweet-savory stew.
ingredients: 1 large whole pumpkin or squash, about 2 kg
instructions: Heat oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Cut a lid from the squash, remove seeds and bake cut-side down for 45–60 minutes until just tender but still holding shape.
Meanwhile brown beef in oil in a pot. Add onion and pepper and cook 6 minutes; stir in tomatoes and stock and simmer 40 minutes.
Add potatoes, pumpkin cubes and corn; simmer 25–30 minutes until tender and sauce is thick. Season.
Set squash upright in a baking dish, fill with stew and bake uncovered 15 minutes. Serve portions with some softened squash.
recipes.sides: Serve with bread and a simple salad.
recipes.substitutions: Cook the stew entirely in a pot if no suitable whole squash is available; the baked shell is a presentation variation.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate stew and squash separately within 2 hours; use within 3 days and reheat thoroughly.
recipes.safety: Handle the hot squash carefully and support it in a baking dish. Ensure beef is tender and the filling hot throughout.

recipes.name: Ensalada criolla
recipes.description: A fresh side salad of tomato, onion and pepper dressed simply with oil and vinegar.
instructions: Slice tomatoes into wedges. Thinly slice onion and soak it in cold water for 10 minutes if you prefer a milder bite; drain well.
Thinly slice green pepper and combine with tomato and onion in a bowl.
Whisk oil and vinegar with a pinch of salt and pepper. Pour over vegetables and toss gently.
Rest 10 minutes, add parsley if using and serve.
recipes.sides: Serve alongside asado, choripán, milanesa or empanadas.
recipes.substitutions: Use white or spring onion; omit pepper if unavailable. Adjust vinegar to taste.
recipes.storage: Best freshly dressed. Refrigerate undressed vegetables and use the same day.
recipes.safety: Wash vegetables under running water and use a clean knife and board.

recipes.name: Rabas
recipes.description: Lightly floured squid rings fried quickly until crisp and served with lemon.
ingredients: 500 g cleaned squid tubes, thawed if frozen
instructions: Pat squid thoroughly dry and slice into 1 cm rings. Season flour with salt and pepper.
Heat 4 cm oil in a deep pan to 180°C. Dredge squid lightly in flour and shake off excess.
Fry in small batches for 60–90 seconds until pale gold; do not overcrowd or overcook.
Drain on a rack, squeeze lemon over and serve immediately.
recipes.sides: Serve as a shared starter with lemon and a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use prepared calamari rings; thaw fully in the refrigerator and dry well.
recipes.storage: Best served immediately; fried squid toughens on reheating.
recipes.safety: Thaw seafood in the refrigerator, keep it separate from ready-to-eat foods and take care with hot oil.

recipes.name: Pastelitos de batata
recipes.description: Crisp layered holiday pastries filled with sweet potato paste, a companion variation to quince pastelitos.
instructions: Mix flour and salt. Rub in butter, add water gradually and knead until smooth. Cover and rest 20 minutes.
Roll thinly, brush with oil and fold in thirds. Turn and roll once more; rest 10 minutes, then roll to 3 mm and cut 24 squares.
Put a cube of dulce de batata on 12 squares. Brush edges with water, top at an angle with remaining squares and press around filling.
Fry in 170°C oil in small batches until puffed and golden. Drain and brush lightly with syrup if desired.
recipes.sides: Serve warm with mate or tea.
recipes.substitutions: Quince paste can be used for the classic membrillo filling. Use a thermometer to keep frying oil steady.
recipes.storage: Best on the day; keep cooled pastries loosely covered and re-crisp in a low oven.
recipes.safety: Hot oil can cause severe burns. Keep the pot stable, fry in small batches and never leave it unattended.

recipes.name: Empanadas riojanas
recipes.description: Baked empanadas with beef, onion, potato, egg and olive; regional seasoning and fillings vary by household.
instructions: Boil potato dice 5 minutes, drain. Cook onion in oil until soft, add beef and brown completely.
Stir in paprika, cumin, potato, salt and pepper. Cool filling fully, then fold in egg and olives.
Heat oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Fill pastry rounds, moisten edges, fold and crimp securely.
Bake 15–18 minutes until golden and hot inside. Rest briefly before eating.
recipes.sides: Serve with a fresh salad and mild chilli sauce.
recipes.substitutions: Use minced beef if hand dicing is not practical. Family recipes vary in potato and olive amounts.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate cooked empanadas promptly and use within 3 days. Reheat in an oven until hot.
recipes.safety: Cool filling before assembly; refrigerate while preparing multiple trays. Cook beef thoroughly.

recipes.name: Tortilla santiagueña
recipes.description: A large flour tortilla cooked on a griddle, traditionally made with fat and eaten with mate or as a simple meal.
instructions: Mix flour and salt. Rub in lard until evenly distributed.
Add warm water gradually and knead 6 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest 15 minutes.
Divide into 6 portions and roll each into a thin round about 20 cm wide.
Cook on a hot dry griddle 2–3 minutes per side until browned spots appear and the centre is cooked. Keep wrapped in a cloth.
recipes.sides: Eat warm with mate, cheese or leftover meat.
recipes.substitutions: Use vegetable shortening or oil for a meat-free version. Add water gradually to avoid sticky dough.
recipes.storage: Wrap cooled tortillas and keep for 1 day; reheat on a dry griddle.
recipes.safety: Use a stable hot griddle and turn flatbreads with tongs.

recipes.name: Bife de chorizo a la plancha
recipes.description: A thick sirloin steak simply seared and rested, a common parrilla and home meal.
ingredients: 2 sirloin steaks, 250 g each and 3 cm thick
instructions: Pat steaks dry and let stand out of the refrigerator for 15 minutes. Heat a heavy skillet until very hot.
Rub steaks with oil and season with salt. Sear 3–4 minutes per side, adjusting for thickness and desired doneness.
Check with a thermometer for the chosen safe doneness; transfer to a warm plate and rest 5–8 minutes.
Add pepper and serve with lemon wedges.
recipes.sides: Serve with fries, salad or grilled vegetables; chimichurri is optional.
recipes.substitutions: Use another thick sirloin or strip steak. Cooking time varies with cut and pan heat.
recipes.storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 3 days.
recipes.safety: Use a clean plate and utensils after cooking; avoid returning cooked steak to a raw-meat plate.

recipes.name: Chocotorta
recipes.englishName: Chocolate biscuit and dulce de leche cake
recipes.description: A no-bake layered cake of chocolate biscuits and a cream-cheese and dulce de leche filling.
instructions: Beat cream cheese until smooth. Fold in dulce de leche until evenly combined.
Dip biscuits quickly in cooled milk or coffee; do not soak until they collapse.
Arrange a layer of biscuits in a dish, spread with filling and repeat, finishing with filling.
Cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours until the layers soften and cake holds together. Dust with cocoa if desired.
recipes.sides: Serve cold with coffee or fruit.
recipes.substitutions: Use plain tea biscuits if chocolate biscuits are unavailable; add cocoa between layers for a stronger chocolate taste.
recipes.storage: Keep covered and refrigerated; use within 3 days.
recipes.safety: Keep dairy dessert chilled and do not leave it at room temperature for extended periods.

recipes.name: Locro de verduras
recipes.description: A meat-free homestyle locro with hominy, beans, squash and vegetables, inspired by regional corn stews.
ingredients: 250 g dried white hominy corn, soaked overnight
150 g dried white beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Drain soaked hominy and beans. Put in a large pot with onion, carrot and vegetable stock; bring to a boil, then simmer gently 90 minutes.
Stir often and add hot water if needed. Add pumpkin and potato and simmer another 60–75 minutes until beans and corn are tender.
Mash some pumpkin against the side of the pot to thicken the broth. Stir in paprika, cumin and pepper.
Taste, adjust seasoning and serve hot with chilli oil offered separately.
recipes.sides: Serve with bread and chopped spring onion.
recipes.substitutions: Use canned white beans, adding them during the final 30 minutes. Keep hominy corn for its characteristic texture.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze. Reheat to a full simmer, stirring often.
recipes.safety: Soak dried beans in the refrigerator in warm weather and cook fully until tender; do not serve undercooked beans.
